units.tr: 20. Does a copy of a rescript prove as much as the authentic one?

units.la: 21. An error in constructione vitiet rescriptum?
units.tr: 21. Does an error in construction vitiate a rescript?

units.la: 22. An rescriptum Principis strictè sit sumendum?
units.tr: 22. Is a rescript of the Prince to be taken strictly?

units.la: 23. Utrum ius tertio quæsitum per Principem possit auferri.
units.tr: 23. Whether a right acquired by a third party can be taken away by the Prince.

units.la: 2. Verum tamen quia maxime Principis cernitur potestas, in ferendis legibus, abrogandisque, ideo paulo uberius, de jure à Principe constituto, agere decrevi. Eo nomine veniunt diversa; quæ generali appellatione Placita, & Constitutiones, appellantur: cum quod Principi placuit, legis habeat vigorem. Ut id tamen accipiendum sit de tali Principe, qui sic animum suum instituit, ut nihil velit, nisi quod justum, honestum, reipublicæ utile, atque salutare: cuique nihil lubeat, nisi quod liceat. Neque enim eundem aliam à Populo tanquam causâ secundâ mediante potestatem accepisse affirmare ausim. Præsertim cum Principem non in alios usus à Deo causâ secundâ mediante Reipublicæ datum esse testetur ipse Imperator. Et alibi Principis authoritatem à Jovis dependere auctoritate fateatur. l. 1. D. de Princ. Constit. Arg. l. 2. D. eod. l. 4. Cod. de leg. l. 3. Cod. de Testam. Nov. 73. Hottom. ad §. 7. Inst. Jur. Nat. Gent. Civil. Balduin. comm. ad. d §. 7. Zoes. D. Constit. Princ. Perez. Cod de leg. num. 4.
units.tr: 2. Yet because the power of the Prince is seen most in the making and abrogating of laws, I have decided to treat somewhat more fully of law established by the Prince. Under this heading come various things, which are called by the general name placita and constitutiones, since what has pleased the Prince has the force of law. This must, however, be understood of such a Prince as so orders his mind that he wills nothing but what is just, honourable, useful and salutary to the commonwealth, and who is pleased by nothing except what is lawful. For I would not venture to affirm that he received his power from the People as an intervening secondary cause; especially since the Emperor himself testifies that the Prince was given by God to the commonwealth, through a secondary cause, for no other purpose, and elsewhere admits that the authority of the Prince depends on the authority of Jove. l. 1. D. de Princ. Constit. Arg. l. 2. D. eod. l. 4. Cod. de leg. l. 3. Cod. de Testam. Nov. 73. Hottom. ad §. 7. Inst. Jur. Nat. Gent. Civil. Balduin. comm. ad d. §. 7. Zoes. D. Constit. Princ. Perez. Cod de leg. num. 4.

units.la: 3. Nec tamen omnia, quæ Principi placent, licet non iniqua sint, legis habent vigorem, nisi etiam Principi fuerit animus τὸ κοινὸν τὸν νομοθέτημα. id est, quod ei visum fuerit, ut loquitur Alber. esse legem & legis habere vigorem. Adeoque aliquid constituerit non temere aut temerarie, verum de consilii sui sententiâ. l. 8. Cod. de leg. & const. Nov. Leon. 92. Cujac. Parat. Cod. eod. Alber. Gent. disp. de libr. jur. canon. p. mihi. 21. Balduin. loc. ante alleg. Merul. prax. civil. libr. 1. tit. 4 cap. 1. art. 11. 18. & cap. 4. artic. 1. Zyp. Jur. Pontif. Anal. Enarrat. libr. 1. tit. de Constit. p. 11. Perez. Cod. de leg. num. 4. Zoes. loc. alleg. num. 2. Tulden. tit. Cod. de leg. num. 3.
units.tr: 3. Yet not everything that pleases the Prince has the force of law, even if it is not unjust, unless the Prince also has the intention of the common purpose of legislation [τὸ κοινὸν τοῦ νομοθετήματος], that is, as Albericus puts it, what has seemed good to him to be law and to have the force of law. Thus he should lay down something not rashly or carelessly, but by the judgment of his considered counsel. l. 8. Cod. de leg. & const. Nov. Leon. 92. Cujac. Parat. Cod. eod. Alber. Gent. disp. de libr. jur. canon. p. mihi. 21. Balduin. loc. ante alleg. Merul. prax. civil. libr. 1. tit. 4 cap. 1. art. 11. 18. & cap. 4. artic. 1. Zyp. Jur. Pontif. Anal. Enarrat. libr. 1. tit. de Constit. p. 11. Perez. Cod. de leg. num. 4. Zoes. loc. alleg. num. 2. Tulden. tit. Cod. de leg. num. 3.

units.la: 4. Placita vero Principum sunt vel generalia, vel specialia, personalia appellata, qualia sunt Privilegia. Illorum species sunt,
units.tr: 4. The pleasures of Princes are either general or special, the latter called personal, such as privileges. Their species are:

units.la: Decretum, Edictum, Oratio, Mandatum, sanctio, Rescripta, subscriptio, Adnotatio, Epistola, Pragmatica sanctio, interlocutio.
units.tr: Decree, edict, oration, mandate, sanction, rescripts, subscription, annotation, epistle, pragmatic sanction, interlocution.

units.la: 5. Decretum est sententia definitiva (de interlocutoriâ post modum agendum) causâ plene cognitâ & partibus cominus constitutis à Principe inter eosdem lata. Ut si in absentem lata sit, non statim vim legis generalis obtineat; eo quod magis ob partis contumaciam lata videatur, quam ob causæ ipsius iniquitatem. §. 7. Instit. de Jur. Nat. Gent. Civil. l. 1. D. de Constit. Princ. l. 3. D. de his que in Test. delent. l. ult. in princ. Cod. de legibus. Arg. l. qui repudiatis. 17. D. de Inoffic. Testam. Balduin. in Comm. §. 7. v. decrevit. Instit. de Jur. Nat Gent. Besold. Oeconom jur. tit. 3. & 4. libr. 1. D. num. 10. in comment. Bocer. Classf. 1. Pand. disp. 3. num. 22. 23.
units.tr: 5. A decree is a definitive sentence (the interlocutory one is to be discussed afterwards), pronounced by the Prince between parties set in person, once the cause has been fully examined, and given between those same parties. So if it is pronounced against an absent party, it does not at once obtain the force of a general law, because it seems to have been given more on account of the party's contumacy than on account of the injustice of the cause itself. §. 7. Instit. de Jur. Nat. Gent. Civil. l. 1. D. de Constit. Princ. l. 3. D. de his que in Test. delent. l. ult. in princ. Cod. de legibus. Arg. l. qui repudiatis. 17. D. de Inoffic. Testam. Balduin. in Comm. §. 7. v. decrevit. Instit. de Jur. Nat Gent. Besold. Oeconom jur. tit. 3. & 4. libr. 1. D. num. 10. in comment. Bocer. Classf. 1. Pand. disp. 3. num. 22. 23.

units.la: 6. Edictum est, quod Princeps ordinarie spontaneo motu, quandoque etiam ad suggestionem alicujus constituit, & jubet ut fiat, atque generaliter observetur. Quasi legem aliquam novam, & jus novum constitueret. Cujus plerumque initium est; Hac perpetuâ, vel, hac perpetuò valiturâ lege sancimus. Quod etiam edictum non sine consensu Senatus (in speciem scil. alicujus libertatis) promulgari debet. l. 3. Cod. de leg. & Constit. l. hac edictali. Cod. de Secund Nupt. - l. 8. Cod. de leg. & const. l. 22. in sin. Cod. Sacrof. Ecclef. l. 1. l. 1. in sin. Cod. Testam. Milit. Theoph. ad §. 7. Instit. de Jur. Nat. Gent. Hottom. ibidem verf. per epistolam constituit. Boer. class. 1. disp. Pand. 3. num. 24. Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. libr. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. num. 5.
units.tr: 6. An edict is what the Prince ordinarily establishes, of his own accord, and sometimes at someone's suggestion, and orders to be done and generally observed, as if he were enacting some new law and new right. Its usual beginning is: "By this perpetual law, or by this law to remain valid forever, we sanction." This edict also ought not to be promulgated without the consent of the Senate (namely in the case of some kind of liberty). l. 3. Cod. de leg. & Constit. l. hac edictali. Cod. de Secund Nupt. — l. 8. Cod. de leg. & const. l. 22. in sin. Cod. Sacrof. Eccles. l. 1. l. 1. in sin. Cod. Testam. Milit. Theoph. ad §. 7. Instit. de Jur. Nat. Gent. Hottom. ibidem verb. per epistolam constituit. Boer. class. 1. disp. Pand. 3. num. 24. Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. libr. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. num. 5.

units.la: 8. Mandatum est, vel constitutio (quod ejus genus, ut huic tanquam speciei subjiciatur. in l. 3. D. colleg. & corpor. l. 4. Cod. incest. Nupt.) vel praeceptum, sive monitum, sive jussum (cum poenâ si conjunctum, sanctio appellata. licet quandoque generaliter illa vox accipiatur.) quod certis personis à Principe datur, veluti Praefectis & Procuratoribus bus, ut laudabiliter partem sibi commissam possint administrare, etiam illis, qui de negotio aliquo cognoscunt, vel illud exequuntur. Taleque præceptum vulgo Commissio appellari solet. Neque nuncii, aut ministris, aut apparitoribus sine tali instrumento, credi solet, aut oportet. §. Sancti Instit. Rer. Divis. Gloss. ibid. tot. tit. Cod. de Mandat. Princ. l. prohibitum. Cod. jur. fisc. l. neminem. Cod. Remilit. l. Prohibitorias. Cod. diversf. offic. Nov. 17. Cujac. Parat. Cod. mand. Princ. Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. lib. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. 6. Christin. 2. decis. 64. Baldus de Angel. in Prato super 1. Cod. tit. 18. ad l. si quis mica, ubi & addit limitationes. vid. Gor. post. advers. ad l. 191 D. off. Præf. p. mihi 275.
units.tr: 8. A mandate is, or an enactment (of which kind this is subordinated to it as a species, l. 3. D. colleg. & corpor.; l. 4. Cod. incest. nupt.), or a precept, whether an admonition or an order (when joined with a penalty it is called a sanction, though that word is sometimes taken in a general sense), which the Prince gives to certain persons, such as prefects and procurators, so that they may administer laudably the part committed to them, and also to those who have some business to deal with or carry it out. Such a precept is commonly called a commission. Nor are messengers, ministers or attendants believed or required to act without such an instrument. §. Sancti Instit. Rer. Divis.; Gloss. ibid.; tot. tit. Cod. de Mandat. Princ.; l. prohibitum. Cod. jur. fisc.; l. neminem. Cod. Remilit.; l. Prohibitorias. Cod. diversf. offic.; Nov. 17.; Cujac. Parat. Cod. mand. Princ.; Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. lib. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. 6.; Christin. 2. decis. 64.; Baldus de Angel. in Prato super 1. Cod. tit. 18. ad l. si quis mica, where he also adds limitations; see Gor. post. advers. ad l. 191 D. off. Praef. p. mihi 275.

units.la: 9. Unde etiam Mandatum, quod ex scripto non constat, nullius est momenti, neque aliter probatur, nisi per scripturam; ut si dicatur secretum, non admittatur l. 1. Cod. de Mand. Princ l. 5. in sin. D. de Jur. Fisc. Cujac. loc. cit. Tuldenus comm. Cod. eod. num. 2. Christin. loc. cit. Exceptis tamen nonnullis casibus, quibus & sine scripto mandatum valet. Puta, si quis ex ore Principis se habere dicat. &c. l. 2. Cod. Mand. Princ. Nov. 113. c. 2. nov. 17. Quod etiam in Legatis obtinere censet Tuldenus, qui licet credentiae literas, uti loquuntur, exhibere tenentur; non tamen mandatum à Principe sibi scripto traditum proferre, ne arcana Reipublicæ vel hostibus, vel aliis pandantur. Tulden. in Cod. tit. de Mand. Princ. num. 3. Per Paschal. de Legatis, c. 59. Plura qui cupiat de Mandatis (quæ etiam vulgo mandamenta appellantur) deque variis eorundem acceptionibus, divisionibus, adeat Mindanum prolixe differentem tract. de Process. libr. 2. c. 1. & seq.
units.tr: 9. Hence also a mandate which does not appear in writing is of no weight, and cannot be proved otherwise than by writing; so that if it is said to be secret, it is not admitted. l. 1. Cod. de Mand. Princ.; l. 5. in sin. D. de Jur. Fisc.; Cujac. loc. cit.; Tuldenus comm. Cod. eod. num. 2.; Christin. loc. cit. There are, however, some exceptions, in which a mandate is valid even without writing: for example, if someone says that he has it from the mouth of the Prince. &c. l. 2. Cod. Mand. Princ.; Nov. 113. c. 2.; nov. 17. Tuldenus thinks this also holds for ambassadors, who, although they are bound to exhibit their letters of credence, as they are called, are not obliged to produce a mandate handed to them in writing by the Prince, lest the secrets of the state be laid open to enemies or others. Tulden. in Cod. tit. de Mand. Princ. num. 3.; through Paschal. de Legatis, c. 59. Whoever wishes more on mandates (which are also commonly called mandamenta), and on their various meanings and divisions, let him consult Mindanus, who treats the matter at length in tract. de Process. libr. 2. c. 1. & seq.

units.la: 10. Verum hic anxie quæsitum utrum mandato Principis omnino parendum sit? Respondeo.
units.tr: 10. But here the question is anxiously raised: must the Prince's mandate be obeyed absolutely? I answer.

units.la: 1. Si quid mandet ipse princeps per se, aut per suos, quod juri civili positivo, & mutabili adversetur, parendum quidem erit de jure, non tamen indistincte. Quia si quid contra jus partis mandaverit, censebitur per subreptionem & obreptionem impetratum esse mandatum. Aut si quid durius vel severius jusserit per 30. dies, qui mandatum exequitur, tenebitur expectare, adeoque differre executionem; quod sperandum sit bonum Principem de severitate quid esse relaxaturum. Neque committitur sacrilegium, si quis non parendo simpliciter, velit de æquitate aut iniquitate rescripti Principalis disputare; propterea quod id velit ipse Princeps, cujus auctoritas a juris & legum, maxime fundamentalium, pendet auctoritate. l. 2. l. ult. Cod. Si contr. jus vel util. l. 2. Cod. de Pæn. l. 4. in sin. Cod. de leg.
units.tr: 1. If the Prince himself, either in person or through his own agents, commands something which is contrary to positive and changeable civil law, it must indeed be obeyed as a matter of law, but not indiscriminately. For if he has commanded anything against the right of a party, the mandate will be deemed to have been obtained by subreption and obreption. Or if he has ordered something harsher or more severe, the one who carries out the mandate shall be bound to wait thirty days, and so defer execution, since it is to be hoped that a good Prince will relax something of the severity. Nor is it a sacrilege if someone, instead of simply obeying, wishes to dispute the equity or iniquity of the princely rescript, because the Prince himself wills it, whose authority depends on the authority of law, and especially of fundamental law. l. 2. l. ult. Cod. Si contr. jus vel util.; l. 2. Cod. de Pæn.; l. 4. in sin. Cod. de leg.

units.la: 2. Si quid Princeps mandet, quod adversetur juri naturæ, adeoque sit turpe, probrosum, aut inhonestum; quod manifeste divino juri, divinis legibus, atque justionibus sit contrarium (id quod tamen non facile præsumendum erit, ne sic semet obedientiæ nativæ Principis subducendi oriatur occasio) nemo mortalium unquam Principi auscultare ejusque iniquis jussionibus parere tenebitur. Rationes, quæ id suadent sunt variæ.
units.tr: 2. If the Prince commands something which is contrary to natural law, and so is base, shameful or dishonourable, or which is manifestly contrary to divine law, to divine statutes and commands (which, however, is not to be presumed easily, lest an occasion arise for withdrawing from the native obedience owed to the Prince), no mortal shall ever be bound to listen to him or obey his unjust commands. There are various reasons that persuade of this.

units.la: 1. Quia Princeps jubendo non facit licitum, quod aliter in conscientia foret illicitum, aut vetando illicitum, quod aliter esset in se licitum, & recte factum. Ut nec justum sit eo ipso, quod quid mandet, aut injustum eo ipso, quod quid prohibeat. Cumque ad illicitum, vel injustum nulla sit obligatio, etiam nemo parentium tale quid imperanti auscultare necesse habet. Ut injuriosa in Deum vox sit, tantum auctoritatis Principi tribuere, quasi ex peccato, siquidem ita velit, possit facere non peccatum; & vice versa, ex non peccato peccatum. Et in parato oporteat stare subditum ut quibuscunque mandatis, cæcâ quâdam obedientiâ, pareat. Ita quippe nihil Principe foret ferocius, ut qui magis esset metuendus, quam ipse Deus. Persuasum enim sibi habet subditus, dum jussui divino paret, illo nihil iniqui contineri. Ut à Deo absolutam postulari obedientiam, sit æquum bonum; ab homine peccatore, sit iniquum. Quo magis mirari jubet Professorem Maresium, pudet referre, sic artem gnatonicam didicisse, ut quod minime Theologum decet, sed aulico Parasitrastro in more positum est, ubique Placentinum velit agere, vix ullibi Veronensem, & quaecunque dicta & facta potentiorum, ad exemplum & regulam referre. Quinimo quicquid magistratus judicat esse honeste factum, id etiam in conscientia & coram Deo licitum atque honestum declarare. Vox equidem Antichristiana, ne dicam tyrannica e Scholis Reformatorum eliminanda. Ut quae Magistratum Papam facit Romanum, eique in conscientias hominum tribuit imperium, qui secundum Canonistas, ex peccato jubendo, facit non peccatum; adeoque dispensare atque disponere valet, contra Mosem, contra Apostolos, etiam ipsum Christum.
units.tr: 1. Because the Prince, by commanding, does not make lawful what would otherwise be unlawful in conscience, nor, by forbidding, make unlawful what would otherwise be lawful in itself and rightly done. So a thing is not just merely because he commands it, nor unjust merely because he forbids it. And since there is no obligation to what is unlawful or unjust, no one is bound to obey one who commands such a thing. It would be an injurious word against God to ascribe so much authority to the Prince that, if he so wished, he could make from sin what is not sin, and conversely from what is not sin, sin. And the subject would have to stand ready to obey whatever mandates with a certain blind obedience. For thus nothing would be more fierce than the Prince, who would be more to be feared than God himself. The subject is indeed persuaded that, while he obeys the divine command, nothing unjust is contained in it. It is just and good that absolute obedience be demanded from God; from a sinful man it is unjust. All the more is one moved to wonder at Professor Maresius, who (I am ashamed to report) has learned the art of the courtier so well that, as is customary for a courtly parasite, which least befits a theologian, he wishes everywhere to play the Placentine, and hardly anywhere the Veronese, and to refer whatever the powerful say and do to example and rule. Indeed, he declares that whatever the magistrate judges to have been honourably done is also lawful and honourable in conscience and before God. That is indeed an Antichristian, not to say tyrannical, voice, and it must be eliminated from the schools of the Reformed. For it makes the magistrate a Roman Pope, and grants him dominion over men's consciences, who, according to the Canonists, by commanding from sin makes not sin, and so is able to dispense and dispose, against Moses, against the Apostles, even against Christ himself.

units.la: 2. Quia cum populus Principi jurat obedientiam, ea lege & conditione id agit, ut salvum maneat jus supremi Moderatoris, qui solus potest salvare & perdere. Et non aliter atque vasallus dum Seniori fidelitatem praestat, excipit Imperatorem, aut supremum Principem, ita & homo Christianus, excipit Deum, cui ante omnia parendum est.
units.tr: 2. Because when the people swear obedience to the Prince, they do so on this condition and stipulation, that the right of the supreme Governor, who alone can save and destroy, remain intact. Just as a vassal, while rendering fealty to his Senior, excepts the Emperor or the supreme Prince, so the Christian man excepts God, to whom obedience is owed before all else.

units.la: 3. Quia quando quid mandat vir Princeps, quod ei fini, quem ipse propositum habet, & habere debet, adversatur; quoque nomine, qua lege & conditione in Principem est electus; tunc equidem illi nativa merito obedientia denegānda. Id quod accidit, si quid mandet, quod divinis præceptis adversatur.
units.tr: 3. Because when the Prince commands something which is contrary to the end that he himself proposes and ought to propose, and to that on account of which, and under which law and condition, he was elected Prince, then natural obedience is rightly to be denied him. This happens if he commands something contrary to divine precepts.

units.la: 4. Quia is ordo naturæ & jurisgentium primævi servandus est, ut ante omnia Deo parendum sit, deinde Patriæ, seu Principi, denique Parentibus. l. 2. D. de Just. & jure. Nam quo finis est ulterior, communior est, & fini ultimo, cætera inferiora tanquam media subordinata censentur, ut per omnia ei inservire debeant, nec minimum ab eo declinare? Et non aliter atque qui in familiâ, servus vicarius, qui erat in peculio servi ordinarii, magis domino parere tenetur, quam ordinario, quod omnes absolute Patrifamilias subsint: ita etiam omnes subditi, qui Principi subjecti, unà cum principe, ut servi Dei Altissimi considerati, licet distinctis assignatis officiis, huic maxime parere necessum habent: ideoque ad hoc maxime advertere, & esse solliciti, ne quid agant, aut ne quid fiat in detrimentum aut contumeliam domini supremi.
units.tr: 4. Because this order of nature and of the primeval law of nations must be observed, that before all things one must obey God, then the fatherland or the prince, and finally parents. For the further an end is, the more common it is, and the other, lower things are regarded as means subordinated to the ultimate end, so that they ought to serve it in every respect and not depart from it in the least. And just as in a household, a vicarious slave, who was in the private property of an ordinary slave, is bound to obey the master more than the ordinary one, because all are absolutely subject to the head of the family, so also all subjects, who are subject to the prince, are bound to obey him above all, together with the prince, considered as servants of the Most High God, although their duties are distinctly assigned; and therefore they must pay especial heed to this and take care that they do nothing, and that nothing is done, to the detriment or dishonour of the supreme Lord.

units.la: 5. Quia cum Princeps limitatum habeat à Deo imperium, non potest absolute quid mandare, sed respectu semper habito ad jussum supremi legislatoris. Ut si quid de jure divino, contra jus divinum disponat, limites sui mandati, suæque jurisdictionis transgrediatur; cui ideo impune non paretur. l. ult. D. de jurisd. Neque enim illi Deus legum divinarum curam aut dispositionem commisit; ut eis derogare, vel abrogare non audeat. Quinimo non aliter atque ministro, aut apparitori non adhibetur fides nisi proferat mandatum, aut jussum judicis: ita etiam Principi contra expressa mandata divina, sicque mandatum suum excedenti, parendum non est. Quo nomine in capitulari addit. Ludovici Imp. c. 9. scribitur, leges imperatorum, non esse supra legem Dei, sed Subtus. Ut iis in tantum sit parendum, in quantum consistit intra obedientiam Deo debitam, non si excedat. Grasswinck. tract. de PraeIud just. & jur. adversf. P. Rebellum lusit. p. 283.
units.tr: 5. Because since the Prince has his dominion limited by God, he cannot command absolutely, but always with respect to the command of the supreme lawgiver. So if he should dispose something concerning divine law contrary to divine law, he transgresses the limits of his mandate and of his jurisdiction, and therefore is not obeyed with impunity. l. ult. D. de jurisd. For God did not commit to him the care or disposition of the divine laws, so that he might dare to derogate from them or abrogate them. Indeed, just as no faith is given to a minister or attendant unless he produces the mandate or order of the judge, so too the Prince, when he issues express divine mandates and thereby exceeds his own mandate, is not to be obeyed. On this account it is written in the capitulary, addit. Ludovici Imp. c. 9., that the laws of the emperors are not above the law of God but beneath it. So they are to be obeyed only in so far as they remain within the obedience owed to God, and not if they exceed it. Grasswinck. tract. de Praeiud just. & jur. adversf. P. Rebellum lusit. p. 283.

units.la: 6. Quia ipsi aulici gnatones, aliique potestatis absolutae propugnatores acerrimi fatentur, Principem mandare non posse, quod juri naturae, id est, immediate conservationi sui ipsius adversatur; ut ei mandanti, abi & suspende te, parendum non sit. Multo itaque minus, si quid mandet, Dei praecepto, ejusque cultui adversum. Cum etiam nostri Conservatio, honori atque gloriae divinae, tanquam fini ultimato sit postponenda. d. l.
units.tr: 6. Because the court flatterers themselves, and other very fierce advocates of absolute power, admit that a prince cannot command what is contrary to the law of nature, that is, to his own immediate preservation, so that one ordered to go and hang yourself need not obey. Much less, then, if he commands something contrary to God's precept and worship. Since our own preservation too must be put second to the honour and glory of God, as to the ultimate end. d. l.

units.la: 2. D. just. & Jur. Non aliter atque de jure civili, servi tenebantur salutem propriam, dominorum saluti postponere. l. 1. §. 28. D. Silaniar. Grot. in Consult. part. 3 jurisc. Batav. consil. 325. n. 32. omnibus quidem mandatis suprernorum magistratuum parendum esse, modo non pugnent cum jure naturali.
units.tr: 2. D. just. & Jur. Just as in civil law, slaves were bound to put their own safety second to the safety of their masters. l. 1. §. 28. D. Silaniar. Grot. in Consult. part. 3 jurisc. Batav. consil. 325. n. 32. Indeed, obedience is due to all commands of the higher magistrates, provided they do not conflict with the law of nature.

units.la: 7. Id quod etiam suadent monita & exempla virorum piorum, qui aliter Principibus obedientissimi, & ad quævis Principum gratiâ subeunda pericula, paratissimi, jure tamen iis parere detrectarunt, si eo ipso juri divino præjudicatum fuisset. Pauca in proscenium adducam, tam veteris, quam novi testamenti libris insparsa. Non equidem quispiam, nisi crudelis, improbaverit factum obstetricum in Ægypto, quæ impium Regis Pharaonis edictum, de pueris masculis Hebræorum necandis, negligentes, Deo quam homini parere maluerunt. Exod. cap. 1. Nec illaudatum factum Obadiæ aulæ præfecti regis Achab, qui non tantum Dei prophetas contra Tyrannicum sui Regis & domini mandatum, non interemit, verum in spelunca abditos aluit, & servavit. 1. Paralip. 18. v. 2. 3. Quinimo in novo testamento Christus salvator, cujus regnum non erat de hoc modo, ut quoad cætera etiam Principibus gentium esset subjectus, invitis nihilominus & reclamantibus Principibus Sacerdotum, propalam in templo prædicationem evangelii, promovit. Johan. c. 9. Quem secuti Apostoli Primoribus Judæorum morem non gesserunt, interminantibus & prohibentibus, ne in posterum Jesum, ejusque doctrinam salutarem prædicarent: quod in concursu potius Deo, quam hominibus obediendum esse judicarent. Actor. 5. v. 29. Plura qui cupiat exempla & axiomata infpiciat loca fcripturæ, fubfequentia, ibidemque commentatores. Ephef. c. 6. v. 1. Coloff. c. 3. v. 22. 1. Petr. c. 2. v. 17. Exod. c. 1. v. 17. 1. Samuel. c. 22. v. 17. Prov. c. 8. v. 15. & c. 24. v. 21. Daniel. c. 3. v. 12. & seqq. Argum. Matth. c. 22. v. 21. vid. Perez. ad tit. Cod. de jure fisci. Christin vol. 1. decis. 130. n. 9. Sichard. de jure Regio Hebræorum c. 4. Theor. 14. p. 104. Daneum Ethic. Christian. libr. 2. c. 12, Amef. Medull. Theol. libr. 2, c. 17. n. 54. & seq. & in explic. analyt. ad 1. Petr. 2. v. 13. Merul. Prax. civil. libr. 1. tit. 4. c. 2. CarpZov. de Reg. Germanor. c. 1. Althus. Polit. c. 18. 19.
units.tr: 7. Which the counsels and examples of pious men also suggest. Although they were most obedient to princes, and most ready to undergo any dangers to win a prince's favour, they nonetheless rightly refused to obey when obedience would have prejudiced divine law. I shall bring forward a few examples, scattered through the books of both the Old and the New Testament. Surely no one but a cruel man would disapprove of the midwives in Egypt, who, disregarding the impious edict of King Pharaoh to kill the male children of the Hebrews, preferred to obey God rather than man. Exod. cap. 1. Nor is the conduct of Obadiah, the steward of King Ahab's household, to be condemned: he not only did not kill the prophets of God, contrary to the tyrannical command of his king and master, but hid them in a cave and kept them alive. 1. Paralip. 18. v. 2. 3. Moreover, in the New Testament, Christ the Saviour, whose kingdom was not of this world, so that in other matters he was subject to the princes of the nations, nevertheless, though the chief priests were unwilling and protested, openly promoted the preaching of the gospel in the temple. Johan. c. 9. The apostles, following him, did not comply with the leaders of the Jews, who threatened and forbade them to preach Jesus and his saving doctrine any more; they judged that God rather than men must be obeyed in this matter. Actor. 5. v. 29. Whoever desires more examples and maxims, let him look at the following passages of Scripture and the commentators on them. Ephef. c. 6. v. 1. Coloff. c. 3. v. 22. 1. Petr. c. 2. v. 17. Exod. c. 1. v. 17. 1. Samuel. c. 22. v. 17. Prov. c. 8. v. 15. & c. 24. v. 21. Daniel. c. 3. v. 12. & seqq. Argum. Matth. c. 22. v. 21. vid. Perez. ad tit. Cod. de jure fisci. Christin vol. 1. decis. 130. n. 9. Sichard. de jure Regio Hebræorum c. 4. Theor. 14. p. 104. Daneum Ethic. Christian. libr. 2. c. 12, Amef. Medull. Theol. libr. 2, c. 17. n. 54. & seq. & in explic. analyt. ad 1. Petr. 2. v. 13. Merul. Prax. civil. libr. 1. tit. 4. c. 2. CarpZov. de Reg. Germanor. c. 1. Althus. Polit. c. 18. 19.

units.la: 8. Quia hæc noftra fententia communis eft & omni omnino juri congrua; Divino, Civili, Canonico. Primum membrũ ex textibus antea allegatis satis est manifestum, quibus addantur. Ephef. c. 6. v. 1. Matth. 26. v. 47. Jud. v. 11. Galat. 1. v. 10. Et qui locus ex veteri testamento non prætereundus est. Mich. c. 6. v. penult. Ubi propheta Israëlitas execratur, & diris devovet, quod statuta & Præcepta Omri custodivissent, & consilia domus Achab, regumque justis per omnia licet iniquis paruissent. Neque in nov. Testam. ullibi excusantur Herodis satellites quod ad ejus jussum infantes bimulos intermisissent. Matt c. 2.
units.tr: 8. Because this our opinion is common and wholly in accord with every kind of law: divine, civil and canon. The first member is sufficiently clear from the texts cited above, to which may be added: Ephef. c. 6. v. 1. Matth. 26. v. 47. Jud. v. 11. Galat. 1. v. 10. And a passage from the Old Testament must not be passed over: Mich. c. 6. v. penult. There the prophet curses the Israelites and devotes them to destruction because they kept the statutes and precepts of Omri and obeyed the counsels of the house of Ahab and of kings who, though wicked in every respect, were lawful rulers. Nor in the New Testament is there anywhere an excuse for Herod's soldiers, who at his command slew the infants of two years old. Matt c. 2.

units.la: Alterum vel ex eo constat, quod rescripta Principum, contra jus, contra publicam utilitatem impetrata & concepta, nullius sint momenti; multo minus si contra jus Dei sint obtenta, cui imperatores placere studeant. l. 2. 3. 4. 7. Cod. Precibus imper. offer. l. 4. 6. Cod. Diverf. rescript. l. ult. Cod. si contra jus vel utilitat. publicø. nov. 8. in init. novell. 14. de lenonibus. Ego in dissert. de Princip. Constit. n. 10. 16. Cujusque imperium ipsi sequuntur nov. 81. c. 2. in sin. Cujusque civitates administrant. Nov. 17. c. 2. nov. 1; 3. in sin. Quo etiam nomine, ante omnia subditos respicere volunt Deum ipsum, dein timorem regis & legis. Nov. 17. c. ult. nov. 80. de quaestor. c. 1. in med. collata cum l. 2. D. de justitia & jur.
units.tr: The second member is established at least by this: rescripts of princes obtained or issued against law or public utility are of no force; much less if they were obtained against the law of God, whom emperors ought to strive to please. l. 2. 3. 4. 7. Cod. Precibus imper. offer. l. 4. 6. Cod. Diverf. rescript. l. ult. Cod. si contra jus vel utilitat. publicø. nov. 8. in init. novell. 14. de lenonibus. I, in my dissertation de Princip. Constit. n. 10. 16. Subjects follow whatever empire they serve. nov. 81. c. 2. in sin. They administer whatever cities they belong to. Nov. 17. c. 2. nov. 1; 3. in sin. For this reason also, the law wishes subjects to look first to God himself, then to the fear of the king and of the law. Nov. 17. c. ult. nov. 80. de quaestor. c. 1. in med. collata cum l. 2. D. de justitia & jur.

units.la: Postremum membrum colligitur ex variis juris canonici capitulis. Quæ quia insignia continent è Patrum scriptis petita, c. si dominus 11. suppleꞏ cautâ, q. 3. hic inseram. Si dominus ea jubet, quæ non sunt adversa scripturis sanctis, subjicitur servus domino. „ Si vero contraria præcipit, magis obediat „ spiritus, quam corporis domino. Si bonum „ est, quod præcipit imperator, & præses, „ jubentis obsequere voluntati: si vero malum, responde ei illud de actubus Apostolorum: obedire oportet Deo magis, quam „ hominibus. & Ambrosius c. sequenti. Julianus imperator, quamvis esset Apostata, „ habuit tamen sub se Christianos milites: „
units.tr: The last member is gathered from various chapters of the canon law. Since these contain notable material taken from the writings of the Fathers, I shall insert them here, c. si dominus 11, suppl. cautâ, q. 3. "If the master commands things which are not contrary to the holy Scriptures, the servant is subject to the master. But if he orders things contrary to them, the spirit must obey rather than the body of the master. If what the emperor or governor commands is good, obey the will of him who commands; but if it is evil, answer him with that saying from the Acts of the Apostles: we ought to obey God rather than men." And Ambrose, in the following chapter: "The emperor Julian, though an apostate, nevertheless had Christians under him as soldiers:

units.la: quibus cum dicebat, producite aciem pro defensione reipublicæ, obediebant ei. Cum autem diceret eis, producite arma in Christianos, tunc cognoscebant imperatorem Cœli. & Augustin. Can. qui resistit ibid. Qui resistit potestati, Dei ordinationi resistit. Sed quid si illud jubeat, quod non debeas facere? Hic sane contemne potestatem timendo potestatem. Ipsos humanarum legum gradus advertite. Si aliquid jusserit Curator, nonne faciendum est? tamen si contra Proconsul jubeat, non utique contemnis potestatem, sed eligis majori servire. Nec hinc debet minor irasci, si major prælata est. Rursus si aliquid ipse proconsul jubeat, & aliud jubeat ipse imperator, numquid dubitatur illo contempto, illi esse serviendum? Ergo si aliud imperator, aliud Deus, quid judicatis? Solve tributum, esto mihi in obsequium: recte, sed non in idolio. In idolio prohibet. Quis prohibet? Major potestas. Da veniam: tu carcerem, ille gehennam minatur. Hic jam tibi assumenda est fides tua tanquam scutum, in quo possis omnia ignita jacula inimici extinguere. &c. sequenti. Imperatores, si in errore essent, (quod absit) præ errore suo contra veritatem leges darent, per quas justi & probarentur, & coronarentur, non faciendo quod illi juberent, quia Deus prohiberet.
units.tr: when he told them, 'Lead out the line in defence of the commonwealth,' they obeyed him. But when he said to them, 'Lead out your arms against the Christians,' then they recognised the emperor of heaven." And Augustine, in the canon qui resistit, same place: "Whoever resists the power resists the ordinance of God. But what if the power commands something you ought not to do? Here indeed you despise the power out of fear of the power. Consider the very grades of human laws. If a curator commands something, must it not be done? Yet if the proconsul commands otherwise, you certainly are not despising the power, but you choose to serve the greater. Nor should the lesser be angry if the greater is preferred. Again, if the proconsul himself commands something, and the emperor commands something else, does anyone doubt that, the former being disregarded, the latter must be served? So if the emperor commands one thing and God another, what do you judge? Pay the tribute, be at my service: rightly so; but not in idol worship. In idol worship he forbids. Who forbids? The greater power. Grant pardon: you threaten prison, he threatens hell. Here your faith must now be taken up as a shield, in which you can extinguish all the fiery darts of the enemy." &c. In the following chapter: "Emperors, if they were in error (which God forbid), because of their error might make laws against the truth, by which the just would be tested and crowned, by not doing what they commanded, since God forbade it.

units.la: „Sicut jusserat Nabuchodonosor, ut aurea „statua adoraretur: quod qui facere noluerunt, Deo talia prohibenti placuerunt. Quando autem imperatores veritatem tenent, pro ipsa contra errorem jubent. „Quod quisquis contempserit, ipse sibi judicium acquirit. Nam & inter homines „poenas luit & apud Deum sortem non habebit, quia hoc facere noluit, quod ei per „cor regis ipsa veritas jussit: sicut ipse Nabuchodonosor postea miraculo salutis trium „puerorum commotis, atque mutatus, pro „veritate contra errorem edictum proposuit, „ut quicunque blasphemarent Deum Sidrac, Misac, & Abdenego, in interitum „irent, & domus eorum in dispersionem. „Et non vultis ut aliquid tale contra vos, „jubeant imperatores Christiani, cum sciant „à vobis in iis quos rebaptizatis, Christum „exsufflari. & post. Julianus extitit infidelis imperator. Nonne extitit Apostata, „iniquus, idololatra? Milites Christiani servierunt imperatori infideli. Ubi venieba„tur ad causam Christi, non agnoscebant „nisi illum, qui in coelo erat. Quando vo„lebat, ut idola colerent, ut thuificarent, „praeponebant illi Deum. Quando autem „dicebat, producite aciem, ite contra illam „gentem, statim obtemperabant. Distin„guebant dominum aeternum à domino „temporali: & tamen subditi erant propter „dominum æternum etiam domino tempo„rali. Plura qui desideret seq. c. perlegat, „ubi non contemnenda huc facientia occur„runt, uti & c. 92. 95.
units.tr: As Nebuchadnezzar commanded that a golden statue be worshipped; those who refused to do so pleased God, who forbade such things. But when emperors hold to the truth, they command things on behalf of the truth against error. Whoever despises this acquires judgment for himself. For he pays the penalty among men and will not have a lot with God, because he refused to do what the truth itself commanded through the heart of the king; just as Nebuchadnezzar himself afterwards, moved and changed by the miracle of the salvation of the three children, issued an edict on behalf of the truth against error, that whoever blasphemed the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego should go to destruction and their houses be laid waste. And do you not want Christian emperors to command something of this sort against you, since they know that you, in those whom you rebaptise, blow out Christ?" And afterwards: "Julian was an unfaithful emperor. Was he not an apostate, wicked, an idolater? Christian soldiers served the unfaithful emperor. Where the cause of Christ was concerned, they acknowledged no one but him who was in heaven. When he wished them to worship idols, to offer incense, they put God before him. But when he said, 'Lead out the line, go against that nation,' they immediately obeyed. They distinguished the eternal Lord from the temporal lord; and yet they were subject to the temporal lord for the sake of the eternal Lord." Whoever desires more may read through the following chapter, where matters not to be despised that bear on this occur, as also in chapters 92 and 95.

units.la: 11. Verum quis quæ sierit, an non in sacrilegii crimen incidant, qui de Principis illâ potestate faciendi aliquid vel omittendi, audent disputare? per l. . Cod. de Crimin. Sacril.
units.tr: 11. But who would ask whether those who dare to dispute whether the Prince may do or omit something by that power do not incur the crime of sacrilege? per l. . Cod. de Crimin. Sacril.

units.la: Resp. 1. Licet id velint nonnulli divinæ majestatis contemptores, adeoque vere Sacrilegi. l. 1. Cod. De Crim. Sacril qui absolutæ favent dominationi, nihil tamen promoverint; cum d.l.3. complectatur casum, qui erat meri juris civilis, adeoque suberat citra omne dubium, Principis potestati; quales erant munerum largitiones, privilegiorum concessiones, aliaque plurima Principi reservata. Quod ita explicatur in l. 5. Cod. de Diverf. Rescript. Cumque ipse poterat in quoscunque, etiam in immerentes conferre dignitates, velle de illo facto Principis non tantum disputare, sed etiam eum nolle, cui concessa erat à Principe dignitas quæpiam Præfecturæ, pro tali agnoscere, id ipsum Sacrilegio comparabatut, in d.l.3. vid. l. 1. Cod. Domest. & Protector. l. 1. Cod. Ut dignit. Ordo Servet. libr. 12. Cravett. consil. 241. n. 20. Menoch. 2. Præsumpt. 10. n. 56.
units.tr: Answer 1. Some contemners of the divine majesty, and therefore truly sacrilegious, may wish this, and they favour absolute domination; but they gain nothing by it, since d.l.3. covers a case that belonged to merely civil law and therefore, beyond all doubt, lay under the power of the Prince. Such were the bestowal of offices, the granting of privileges, and many other matters reserved to the Prince. This is explained in l. 5. Cod. de Diverf. Rescript. And since he could confer dignities on whomever he pleased, even on the undeserving, to wish to dispute that act of the Prince, or to refuse to acknowledge as such the man to whom a Prince had granted some dignity of prefecture, is equated with sacrilege, in d.l.3. see l. 1. Cod. Domest. & Protector. l. 1. Cod. Ut dignit. Ordo Servet. libr. 12. Cravett. consil. 241. n. 20. Menoch. 2. Præsumpt. 10. n. 56.

units.la: Resp. 2. Etsi non facile in disputationem trahenda sit Principis potestas, in iis, quæ ejusdem spectant jurisdictionem; de quibus loquuntur.l 1. 2. Cod. Crimin. Sacril. Gloss. & DD. ibidem. & in c. litteras de Restit. Spoliat. Attamen in iis, quæ absolute Principi subsunt, de ejusdem scientia, voluntate, & intentione disputare, quia dubitare, fas est, l. ex facto D. vulg. & Pupill. Subst. Unde etiam omne mandatum, semper subintellectam habet conditionem, salva justitia, salvo jure cujusque; quod non sit præsumendum Principem, à quo jura proficiscuntur, aliquid velle fieri, quod cum præjudicio vel injuria tertii conjunctum foret. l. rescripta. Cod. Prec. imper. offer. Bald. in l. 1. D. Princ. constit. Ut, si aliquid excedat Principis potestatem quale est honestum, multo magis dubitare liceat, si quid Princeps circa illud decreverit, quamvis certa sit ejus voluntas, & intentio. Cum secundum canonistas, licet Pontifex, quem tamen magis reverentur, quam ipsum Principem, de plenitudine potestatis, & de certa scientia quid mandaverit, ut si quis pareat, oriretur peccatum, aut scandalum, licite possit tali mandato non parere. Quinimo tantum abesse, ut sit reprehendendus, qui jussum Principis iniquum non implet, ut magis etiam sit laudandus scribunt. Imol. & Fel. in c. si quando de Rescript. &c. cum teneamur, ibique Panormit. de Prebend. apud Schenck à Tautenb. viridar. conclus. jurid. concl. 37. p. 289.
units.tr: Answer 2. Although the power of the Prince should not readily be drawn into dispute in those matters which fall within his jurisdiction, of which loquuntur.l 1. 2. Cod. Crimin. Sacril. Gloss. & DD. ibidem. & in c. litteras de Restit. Spoliat. speak, nevertheless in those matters which are absolutely subject to the Prince, it is lawful to dispute about his knowledge, will and intention, because it is right to doubt; l. ex facto D. vulg. & Pupill. Subst. Hence every mandate always carries the tacit condition: saving justice, saving the right of each person. For it is not to be presumed that the Prince, from whom rights proceed, wishes anything to be done that would be joined with prejudice or injury to a third party. l. rescripta. Cod. Prec. imper. offer. Bald. in l. 1. D. Princ. constit. So, if something exceeds the power of the Prince, as what is dishonourable does, it is all the more permissible to doubt whether the Prince has decreed anything about it, even if his will and intention are certain. For according to the canonists, the Pontiff, whom they revere more than the Prince himself, may, from the fullness of power and with certain knowledge, command something which, if anyone obeyed, would give rise to sin or scandal, and it is lawful for him not to obey such a mandate. Indeed, they write that he who does not carry out an unjust command of the Prince is so far from being blameworthy that he is even to be praised. Imol. & Fel. in c. si quando de Rescript. &c. cum teneamur, ibique Panormit. de Prebend. apud Schenck à Tautenb. viridar. conclus. jurid. concl. 37. p. 289.

units.la: 13. Ubi quaesitum, num quivis Principi valeat supplicare? Resp. Servi non possunt, nisi in crimine majestatis, vel pro necessitate domini. l. 4. Cod. de Prec. imper. offer. l. nullus ad l. Jul. Majestat. Forte etiam si quando à dominis opprimuntur in casu l. 2. D. qui sui vel alien. jur. Rei vero Majestatis supplicare non poterunt. Quia nemo pro illis intercedit. l. 5. §. 2. Cod. Ad l. Jul. majest. Haeretici tamen poterunt. l. ult. §, Jed quia gremium Cod. Sum. trinit. Minor à Principe damnatus, nonnisi raro. C. minor. autem. §. si autem. D. Minor.
units.tr: 13. Here it is asked whether anyone may petition the Prince. Answer: slaves may not, except in a charge of treason, or on behalf of their master's need. l. 4. Cod. de Prec. imper. offer. l. nullus ad l. Jul. Majestat. Perhaps also when they are oppressed by their masters in a case of l. 2. D. qui sui vel alien. jur. But those accused of treason may not petition, because no one intercedes for them. l. 5. §. 2. Cod. Ad l. Jul. majest. Heretics, however, may. l. ult. §, Jed quia gremium Cod. Sum. trinit. A minor condemned by the Prince, only rarely. C. minor. autem. §. si autem. D. Minor.

units.la: 14. Quaesitum amplius, utrum Principis rescriptum habuerit olim vigorem legis universalis? Resp. Quia saepissime rescriptum, ob particularem aliquam circumstantiam datur, & ad speciem certam est accommodatum, non videtur generalem continere juris definitionem. Ut meo judicio fuerit adductum vel allegatum sicut hodie solent res judicatae in supremis curiis, allegari. Nisi tamen Princeps voluerit, illud esse ad instar regulae universalis, vel in codicem relatum vim legis acceperit. Ut tamen in ratione interpretandi multum differat à communi lege. Unde argumentum à contrario sensu non facile in rescripto admittendum. l. 2. Cod. de leg. & Constit. Cujac. Parat. Cod eod. Duaren. de condict. indeb. c 6. & ad tit. Cod. Si in Comm. eademque causâ, Donell. 20. comm. 5. & de & de Pignor. c. 6. Vultej. discept. c. 10. Hilli ger. ad Donell. 1. comment cap. 9. Besold oeco- nom. jur. tit. 3. 4. libr. 1. D. ad num. 10. in sin. Zoes. D. de Constit. Princ. num. 4.
units.tr: 14. It is further asked whether a rescript of the Prince formerly had the force of a universal law. Answer: because a rescript is very often given on account of some particular circumstance and is adapted to a certain case, it does not seem to contain a general definition of law. Hence, in my judgment, it is to be adduced or cited, as judgments of the supreme courts are nowadays customarily cited. Unless, however, the Prince wished it to stand as a universal rule, or had it entered into the code and so given it the force of law. Yet in the manner of interpreting it, it differs much from common law. Hence an argument from the contrary sense is not easily admitted in a rescript. l. 2. Cod. de leg. & Constit. Cujac. Parat. Cod eod. Duaren. de condict. indeb. c 6. & ad tit. Cod. Si in Comm. eademque causâ, Donell. 20. comm. 5. & de & de Pignor. c. 6. Vultej. discept. c. 10. Hilli ger. ad Donell. 1. comment cap. 9. Besold oeco- nom. jur. tit. 3. 4. libr. 1. D. ad num. 10. in sin. Zoes. D. de Constit. Princ. num. 4.

units.la: 15. Idem quod de Interlocutione dicendum; quando scil. Princeps, quasi inter aliud agendum, & loquendum, quid constituit. Quod enim in uno negotio ita prolatum, nihil praejudicat in commune. Non magis atq; res judicata aliis nec nocet nec prodest. Nisi tamen satis appareat, hanc fuisse Principis voluntatem, ut ab omnibus in posterum idem servaretur. Forte, si ad senatum missa, ut confirmaretur; si edicti vocabulo nuncupata, si jussa divulgari; si inter alias ejus constitutiones relata. l. 1. D. de Constit. Princ. l. 2. 3. Cod. de leg. & Constit l. 9. §. 3. D. Quod. Met. caus. Balduin. ad §. 7. verf. decrevit. Instit. de jur. nat. Gent. & civil. Duaren. tit. D. de Princ. const. vid. Fabrum in Ration. ad d. l. 1. Connan. 1. Comm. 16. num. 3. Pacium 1. Enant. queft. 17. Zoes. D. de Princ. const. num. 7. Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. libr. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. a num 9. usque ad finem.
units.tr: 15. What is to be said of an Interlocutione is the same: namely, when the Prince, as if while dealing and speaking about something else, lays down something. For what is so stated in one matter prejudices nothing in general, and is no more harmful or helpful to others than a judgment passed in a case. Unless it sufficiently appears that this was the Prince's will, that the same thing be observed by everyone in future. Perhaps if it was sent to the senate to be confirmed; if it was named by the word edict; if it was ordered to be published; if it was included among his other constitutions. l. 1. D. de Constit. Princ. l. 2. 3. Cod. de leg. & Constit l. 9. §. 3. D. Quod. Met. caus. Balduin. ad §. 7. verf. decrevit. Instit. de jur. nat. Gent. & civil. Duaren. tit. D. de Princ. const. vid. Fabrum in Ration. ad d. l. 1. Connan. 1. Comm. 16. num. 3. Pacium 1. Enant. queft. 17. Zoes. D. de Princ. const. num. 7. Wurmser. Nucl. jur. contr. libr. 1. tit. 2. contr. 5. a num 9. usque ad finem.

units.la: 16. Non omne tamen rescriptum a Principe impetratum valet; ne quidem respectu illius negotii quod concernit. Quid si enim per sub & obreptionem sit impetratum? Id est, tacita veritate, vel expresso mendacio. Unde ut excutiatur rescripti veritas, etiam a Sententia, interveniente rescripto lata, provocari poterit. Et si judex non admiserit precum argui falsitatem, in decem libras auri punitur. Nisi tamen aliquo expresso, vel non expresso, Princeps nihilominus rescriptum in gratiam partis concessisset. Quod quale sit, arbitrio judicis est relinquendum, qui id ipsum suo committet examini. Unde etiam rescriptum à judice ratum est habendum, aut improbandum, quod moribus appellatur rescripti interinatio l. 1. D. de Natal. Restit l. pen. Cod. Si contr. jus vel util.public.l.7.Cod. de diverf. Rescript. & Pragm.Sanct. - Nov. 153. l.1.§.1.D.de Appell.l.1.Cod.Eod. - l.1.Cod. si contr.jus vel util.public. - l. puniri.Cod.eod.Cravett.consil. 592. num. 7. 8. Christin. 2. decis.22.
units.tr: 16. Yet not every rescript obtained from the Prince is valid, not even with respect to the matter it concerns. For what if it was obtained by surreptition or obreption? That is, by concealing the truth or by an express lie. Hence, so that the truth of the rescript may be examined, an appeal may be made even from a sentence pronounced on the strength of the rescript. And if the judge has not allowed the falsity of the petition to be argued, he is punished with a fine of ten pounds of gold. Unless, however, the Prince has nevertheless granted the rescript in favour of the party, whether or not something was expressly stated. What this amounts to must be left to the judge's discretion, who will submit it to his own examination. Hence also a rescript is to be held as confirmed or rejected by the judge, which in custom is called the interinatio of the rescript: D. de Natal. Restit., l. pen. Cod. Si contr. jus vel util., l. 7 Cod. de diversis rescriptis et pragmaticis sanctionibus; Nov. 153; l. 1 §1 D. de appellationibus; l. 1 Cod. eod.; l. 1 Cod. si contra jus vel utilitatem publicam; l. puniri Cod. eod.; Cravetta, consil. 592, nn. 7, 8; Christin. 2 decis. 22.

units.la: 17. Hinc quaesitum, utrum surreptio, vel obreptio in beneficiis aut Privilegiis, vitiet gratiam eorum quae impetrata? Resp. quod ita. Mendax enim precator careat impetratis oportet; & qui in leges impingit, earum beneficio censetur indignus. Id quod in tantum verum est, ut qui per mendacium privilegium obtinuit, lege Cornel. de falsa teneatur. l. 2. l. 5. Cod si contr. jus vel util. Public. Argum. l. 37. in sin. D. de Minor l. si quis D. Ad l. Cornel. de falsa. Tiraquell. de Pæn. caus. 44. Schurf. consil. 7. cent. 2. allegati apud Tulden. Cod. Si contr. jus num. 5. ibidemque alii. Christin. 2. decis. 23. Baldax. de Angel. in Prato super tit. Cod. Si contr. jus. ad l. 1. 2. & seq. Barbos. in coll. ad d. l. 5. vid.
units.tr: 17. Hence the question arises whether surreptition or obreption in benefices or privileges vitiates the grace of the things obtained. The answer is that it does. For a lying petitioner ought to be deprived of what he has obtained, and one who runs against the laws is considered unworthy of their benefit. This is so true that one who has obtained a privilege by lying is liable under the Lex Cornelia on forgery: l. 2, l. 5 Cod. Si contra jus vel utilitatem publicam; argument from l. 37 in fine D. de minoribus; l. si quis D. ad legem Corneliam de falsis; Tiraquell. de poenis causarum 44; Schurf. consil. 7 cent. 2, cited in Tulden. Cod. Si contra jus, n. 5, and there others; Christin. 2 decis. 23; Baldus de Angelis in Pratum super tit. Cod. Si contra jus, ad l. 1, 2 et seq.; Barbosa in coll. ad d. l. 5, see.

units.la: Martin.Uran.Tom. I. consil. 19. num. 44. & seq.
units.tr: Martin.Uran.Tom. I. consil. 19. num. 44. & seq.

units.la: 19. Non itidem valet rescriptum, si lite pendente vel post sententiam sit petitum, Nisi tamen adhoc ipsum, ut edantur acta vel sententia, vel alius associetur judex, vel ut terminetur causa, vel ut citius ipsa finiatur. Auth. in medio litis non fieri sacras. form. §. super hoc. nov. 131. Non etiam, Si non sit adjecta clausula: si preces veritate nitantur. Quod tamen jure canonico secus est. Si forte per rescriptum justitiae secundum leges administratio tardetur, impediaturve. Generaliter non valet rescriptum, si impetratum super eo quod oblatis precibus postulari prohibitum est. Nisi tamen prohibitionis in rescripto facta sit mentio: tit. Cod. ut lite pend. Nov. 82. 113. d. Nov. 113. c. 1. l. 2. Cod. ut lit. Pend. l. ult. Cod. de Diverf. Rescript. c. 2. de Rescript. d. Nov. 113. l 2. l. 5. Cod. de Prec. Imp. offer. Cujac. Parat. Cod. hic. Cravett. consil. 502. num. 60. & seq. & consil. 730. Tesaur. quæst. Forens. libr. 1. quæst. 4. Christin. vol. 2. decif. 70. num. 3. 4. Tulden. Cod. Si contr. jus. num 4. & ult. Baldaxar de Angel. Pratum super Cod. libr. 1. tit. 23. ad L 7.
units.tr: 19. Likewise a rescript is not valid if it was sought while a suit is pending or after sentence has been given, unless it is sought for this very purpose: that the acts or the sentence be produced, or another judge be associated, or that the case be ended, or that it be ended more quickly. Auth. in medio litis non fieri sacras. form. §. super hoc. nov. 131. Nor is it valid if the clause si preces veritate nitantur has not been added. This, however, is otherwise under canon law. If by chance a rescript delays or hinders the administration of justice according to the laws, it is not valid. In general a rescript is not valid if it was obtained on a matter which it was forbidden to request by the petitions presented. Unless, however, mention of the prohibition is made in the rescript. tit. Cod. ut lite pend. Nov. 82. 113. d. Nov. 113. c. 1. l. 2. Cod. ut lit. Pend. l. ult. Cod. de Diverf. Rescript. c. 2. de Rescript. d. Nov. 113. l 2. l. 5. Cod. de Prec. Imp. offer. Cujac. Parat. Cod. hic. Cravett. consil. 502. num. 60. & seq. & consil. 730. Tesaur. quæst. Forens. libr. 1. quæst. 4. Christin. vol. 2. decif. 70. num. 3. 4. Tulden. Cod. Si contr. jus. num 4. & ult. Baldaxar de Angel. Pratum super Cod. libr. 1. tit. 23. ad L 7.

units.la: 20. Ponatur rescriptum aliquod esse impetratum, idque nihil vitii contineat, an exemplum ejusdem, an potius authenticum judici insinuandum erit? Resp. Posterius affirmandum. Quid si post annum demum intentatum aut insinuatum? Nihil obstabit, quo minus effectum sortiatur. Secus quam obtinere volunt de jure canonico: Quo etiam distinguunt inter rescriptum gratiæ & justitiæ. Quasi illud fit perpetuum, hoc annale. l. 3. Cod. de diverf. Rescript. l. 1. Cod. de fid. instrum. Christin. vol. 2. Decif. 78. num. 5. 6. ubi addit limitationes. Baldaxar de Angel. in Prato ad tit. Cod. de Rescript. l. 3. l. 2. Cod. de Diverf. Rescrip. l. 2. & ult. Cod. Theodos. eod. Perez. Cod. hic. num. 4. Tulden. tit. Cod. eod. num. 2. Qui dissensum inter jus can. & civ. non admittit. vid. Christin. 2. vol. Decif. 78. 79. Bald. de Angel. libr. all. ad l. 2. Cod. de Rescript. Christin. d. vol. decif. 77. num. 2. 3. & decif. 80. num. 3. & 6. Faber Cod. libr. 1, tit. 12. desin. 6. Perez. loc. cit.
units.tr: 20. Suppose that some rescript has been obtained and contains nothing faulty: must a copy of it be shown to the judge, or rather the authentic original? The answer: the latter must be affirmed. What if it is only sued upon or presented after a full year? Nothing will stand in the way of its taking effect. This is contrary to what the canon law wishes to maintain, and it also distinguishes between a rescript of grace and one of justice, as if the former were perpetual and the latter lasted a year. l. 3. Cod. de diverf. Rescript. l. 1. Cod. de fid. instrum. Christin. vol. 2. Decif. 78. num. 5. 6. ubi addit limitationes. Baldaxar de Angel. in Prato ad tit. Cod. de Rescript. l. 3. l. 2. Cod. de Diverf. Rescrip. l. 2. & ult. Cod. Theodos. eod. Perez. Cod. hic. num. 4. Tulden. tit. Cod. eod. num. 2. Qui dissensum inter jus can. & civ. non admittit. vid. Christin. 2. vol. Decif. 78. 79. Bald. de Angel. libr. all. ad l. 2. Cod. de Rescript. Christin. d. vol. decif. 77. num. 2. 3. & decif. 80. num. 3. & 6. Faber Cod. libr. 1, tit. 12. desin. 6. Perez. loc. cit.

units.la: 21. Quid si tamen error aliquis in litteris, in constructione sit commissus, anne rescriptum vitiabitur? Resp. Si rescriptum in substantialibus sit legitimum, modicus ille desectus non tollet rescripti effectum, aut adferet ullum impedimentum. Idem quod dicendum, si vitium aliquod occurrat in latinitate. Præsertim cum rescripta plurima imperatorum ante aliquot secula illatinas contineant tincant phrases & voces. Idem quod affirmandum de errore in nomine commisso. c. 11. de fid. instrum. & Gloss. ibid. Arg. l. 1. §. 5. D. de Hered. instit. l. 7. l. 15. l. 24. Cod. de Testam. l. 21. Cod. de leg. Arg. dd. ll. D. D. apud Panorm. in c. ad audientiam manifestum, v. de Rescript. all apud Specham. diss. centur. 1 Quaest. jur. 75. -- Argum l. antepen. D. de judic. l. in vindicationibus D. de Cont. Empt. l. si in nomine D. verb. Oblig. Martin. Uran. tom. 1. consil. 19. num. 32. & seqq. Pancirol. Thesaur. var. lection c. 77. vid. Prolixè Alciat. in Praxi juris utriusque de Except. adversus Rescript. p. 109. usque ad p. 118
units.tr: 21. What if, however, some error in the wording or construction has been committed? Will the rescript then be invalidated? Answer: if the rescript is sound in its substantial points, that slight defect will not defeat its effect or create any obstacle to it. The same is to be said if some fault occurs in the Latinity, especially since very many rescripts of the emperors from some centuries ago contain unlatinate phrases and words. The same must be affirmed of an error committed in a name. c. 11. de fid. instrum. and Gloss ibid. Argument from l. 1 §. 5 D. de Hered. instit., l. 7, l. 15, l. 24 Cod. de Testam., l. 21 Cod. de leg. Argument from the same laws: the doctors cited by Panormitanus in c. ad audientiam manifestum, v. de Rescript.; also by Specham., diss. centur. 1, Quaest. jur. 75. Argument from l. antepen. D. de judic., l. in vindicationibus D. de Cont. Empt., l. si in nomine D. verb. Oblig. Martinus Uranius, tom. 1, consil. 19, num. 32 and following. Pancirollus, Thesaur. var. lection c. 77. See at length Alciatus, in Praxi juris utriusque, de Except. adversus Rescript., pp. 109 to 118.

units.la: 22. Quid si rescriptum Principis sit generale, an extendetur ad ea, quae vel juri communi non congruenter, vel difficulter Principi concederet? Respondeo, quia hoc respectu rescriptum Principis censetur esse stricti juris, verba ejus presse sequemur, nec ea supplicationi convenienter extendemus, ne quidem ex identitate rationis. Praesertim si ille casus, in quo eadem subest ratio, jure communi sit decisus. l. 1. §. 5. & 10. 16. D. ne quid in loc. Public. Bald. in l. 1. D. Constit. Princ. Alciat. 3. Praesumpt. 12. Cravett. consil. 172. num. 2. & 4. & consil. 387. & consil. 591. num. 77. & consil. 730. Faber in Cod. tit. de leg. & Constit. Barbof. coll. in l. 6. Cod. de Precibus Imper. offer. num. 3. & 5. Gotefred. in comment. ad d. l. 1. Christin. volum. 2. decis. 22. num. 4. ibidemque alii. Tulden. ad tit. Cod. si contr. jus vel util. Publicum. 3.
units.tr: 22. But what if a rescript of the Prince is general: will it extend to those things which would be granted by the common law not agreeably, or which the Prince would grant only with difficulty? I answer: in this respect a rescript of the Prince is held to be of strict law, and we shall follow its words closely, nor shall we extend them in accordance with the supplication, not even by reason of an identical ground. Especially if that case, in which the same reason lies, has been decided by the common law. l. 1. §. 5. & 10. 16. D. ne quid in loc. Public. Bald. in l. 1. D. Constit. Princ. Alciat. 3. Praesumpt. 12. Cravett. consil. 172. num. 2. & 4. & consil. 387. & consil. 591. num. 77. & consil. 730. Faber in Cod. tit. de leg. & Constit. Barbof. coll. in l. 6. Cod. de Precibus Imper. offer. num. 3. & 5. Gotefred. in comment. ad d. l. 1. Christin. volum. 2. decis. 22. num. 4. and the others there. Tulden. ad tit. Cod. si contr. jus vel util. Publicum. 3.

units.la: 23. Verum poteritne Princeps suo rescripto jus tertio quaesitum auferre? Respondeo, non id poterit nec debebit, & ideo non praesumitur hoc voluisse, ut rescriptum quo tale quid imperatum, non valeat. Quo tamen casu ratio status, publica utilitas hoc suadet, sic id facere debebit, ut quod incommodi, vel damni suo rescripto dedit, vel intulit, alio quo commodo, vel utilitate compensET.
units.tr: 23. But can the Prince by his rescript take away a right acquired by a third party? I answer: he neither can nor ought to do so, and therefore it is not presumed that he intended that a rescript by which such a thing is commanded should be void. Yet in such a case the reason of state and public utility suggest that he ought to act so that whatever inconvenience or loss he has given or caused by his rescript is compensated by some other advantage or utility.
