There is, however, a case to be noted: if the ward has gone to Leiden without the consent of his guardians or of the orphans' chamber, and this seems to have been done in fraud of the statute, then the statute of Rotterdam ought to retain its force. Consultation of the Batavian jurists, part I, consil. 152, and the authorities cited there; Bartolus, Panormitanus, Boerius, Mascardus; see a similar case in a testator's cause in Peckius, De Testam. Conjug., lib. 4, cap. 29, n. 2; Groenewegen in notes on Grotius, Introd. jur. Holl., lib. 2, part 26, at the end; see also in a similar matter Christianus Rodenburg, d. tract. cap. 1, n. 5, and cap. 2, part ult., tit. 2; Simon van der Leeuwen, Paratit. jur. novissi., lib. 3, part 3, cap. 4, n. 3.

units.la: 11. Verum, quid de nominibus & actionibus statuendum erit? Respondeo, quia proprie loquendo, nec mobilium nec immobilium veniunt appellatione. Etiam vere non sunt in loco, quia incorporalia. l. 3. in init. D. pro socio. l. Gajus. 86. in princ. D. leg. 2. init. instit. de Rebus corpor. & incorp. Ideo non sine distinctione res temperari poterit. Aut igitur realis erit actio, tendens ad immobilia, & spectabitur statutum loci situs immobilium. Aut erit actio realis spectans mobilia, & idem servandū erit quod de mobilibus dictum est. Aut erit actio personalis sive ad mobilia, sive ad immobilia pertinens; quae cum inhaereat ossibus personae, statutum loci creditorum aestimari debebit. l. si quis ergo casus. D. de Pecul. l. 3. D. pro socio. l. 47. iup 2. D. Admin. tutel. l. 100. D. de solut. lex. conf. 16. libr. 1. n. 2. 3. Peck. de Testam. Conjug. libr. 5. c. 30. n. 3. Petrus Wesemb. conf. 1. n. 67. Mev quaest. Prælim. 6. ad jus Lubec. n. 25. & seq. Michael Nizol. Alleg. 19. n. 55. vid. Sand. 4. tit. 4. def. 6. per tradita à Covarr. 2. variar. Resol. 3. Christin. vol. 2. decis. 60. Decis. Capell. Tholos. 316.
units.tr: 11. But what is to be decided concerning debts and actions? I answer: strictly speaking, debts belong neither to movables nor to immovables by name, and since they are incorporeal they are not truly located anywhere (l. 3, in init., D. pro socio; l. Gajus 86, in princ., D. leg. 2; init., Instit. de rebus corpor. et incorp.). Therefore the matter cannot be settled without distinction. Either the action is real and aims at immovables, and the statute of the place where the immovables lie is to be considered; or it is a real action concerning movables, and what has been said of movables must be observed; or it is a personal action, whether concerning movables or immovables, and since it adheres to the person's bones, the statute of the creditor's place ought to be reckoned (l. si quis ergo casus, D. de Pecul.; l. 3, D. pro socio; l. 47, in fine, D. Admin. tutel.; l. 100, D. de solut.; Lex conf. 16, lib. 1, nn. 2, 3; Peckius, De Testam. Conjug., lib. 5, c. 30, n. 3; Petrus Wesembecius, conf. 1, n. 67; Mevius, quaest. Praelim. 6; on the Lübeck law, n. 25 et seq.; Michael Nizolius, Alleg. 19, n. 55; see Sandérus, 4, tit. 4, def. 6, after Covarruvias, 2 variar. resol. 3; Christinaeus, vol. 2, decis. 60; Decis. Capell. Tholos. 316.)

units.la: 12. Nonnunquam tamen quantum ad onus administrationis, curam & sollicitudinem, ex patrimonio loci contractus censentur, vel ejus loci, in quem destinata est solutio, de quibus in seqq. vid. tamen Salicet, ad l.
units.tr: 12. Sometimes, however, as regards the burden of administration, care and concern, contracts are reckoned to belong to the patrimony of the place, or of that place to which payment is destined, about which more in what follows. But see Salicetus on l.

units.la: 1. Cod. sum. Trinit. n. 14. in med.
units.tr: 1 Cod. sum. Trinit. n. 14. in the middle.

units.la: 13. An quod de actionibus, etiam de annuis reditibus statuendum erit, quos moriens in diversis reliquit Provinciis, ubi variant, statuta? Respondeo, licet Besoldus illorum nomine velit neminem dici posse subjectum: quia tamen adinstar actionum vel mobilibus vel immobilibus annumerari poterunt, etiam adhibitâ subsequenti distinctione terminanda erit quaestio. Vel enim talium reddituum nomine sunt affecta immobilia, id est super immobilibus sunt constituti, & immobilibus erunt adscribendi, adeoque statutum loci situs spectabitur, vel immobilia afsecta non sunt illis redditibus, tamque mobilibus poterunt accenseri, atq; adeo statutū loci personæ, cujus illi sūt reditus, inspici debebit.
units.tr: 13. Must the same be decided for annual rents, which a dying person left in various provinces where the statutes differ? I answer: although Besoldus would have it that no one can be called the subject of those rents, nevertheless, since they can be counted among movables or immovables in the manner of actions, the question must be settled by the following distinction. For either the immovables are charged with such rents, that is, the rents are constituted upon immovables and must be classed as immovables, and then the statute of the place where the property lies will be regarded; or the immovables are not charged with those rents, and the rents may be counted as movables, and then the statute of the place of the person to whom the rents belong ought to be consulted.

units.la: An vero reditus annui à Provinciis, vel civitatibus debiti, immobilibus sint annumerandi, non id ausim affirmare, licet sint qui id tueantur; quod ea sententia curiarum arrestis sit confirmata. Etiam nuperâ ordin. Ultraj. decis. Ann. 1659. April. 14. artic. 12. Malim tamen (neque enim hæc ordin. nostrorum constitutio ubique obtinet) distinguere inter illos reditus, quorum nomine 40. nummus solvitur, & quorum nomine nihil penditur. Ut illi immobilibus, hi mobilibus sint annumerandi. Arg. l. pen. Cod. Agricol. Censit. vid. Boër. quæst. 119. Sneidwin. ad §. retinendæ. instit. de interdict. n. 7. & seq. Gail. 2. obs. 11. Radelant. decis. Cur. Ultraj. 88. & 116. Petrum Wesemb. Consil. 1. Qui tamen inter præteritos & suturos reditus distinguit. n. 53. & seqq. Vid. Anton. Matth. tract. de Auction. libr. 1. cap. 3. in sin. Christin. vol. 2. decis. 61. Rodenb. de Jure Conjug. tit. 2. c. 2. p. 34. 35. n. 3. Paulo aliter Peck. libr. 5. de Testam. conjug. cap. 30. n. sin. in sin, ibique varii.
units.tr: Whether annual rents owed by provinces or cities are to be counted as immovables, I would not venture to affirm, although there are those who defend this, since that opinion has been confirmed by decisions of the courts. The recent ordinance of Utrecht, decision of 14 April 1659, article 12, also says so. I would prefer, however (for this ordinance of our people does not hold everywhere), to distinguish between those rents for which 40 nummi are paid and those for which nothing is paid: that the former be counted as immovables and the latter as movables. By argument from l. pen. Cod. Agricol. Censit. See Boër, question 119; Sneidwin on the §. retinendae, Institutes on interdicts, n. 7 and following; Gail, 2 obs. 11; Radelant, decisions of the Court of Utrecht, 88 and 116; Petrus Wesembeccius, Consilium 1, who, however, distinguishes between past and future rents, n. 53 and following. See Antonius Matthaeus, treatise On Auctions, book 1, chapter 3, at the end; Christinaeus, vol. 2, decision 61; Rodenburg, On the Law of Marriage, title 2, chapter 2, pp. 34, 35, n. 3. Peck, book 5 On Wills of Spouses, chapter 30, n. at the end, and the various authors cited there, differs somewhat.

units.la: 14. Quando autem actiones vel reditus annui, vel servitutes & jura, mobilium aut immobilium nomine veniant, explicat Gabriel comm. opin. libr. 6. de verb. signif. concl. 7. 8.
units.tr: 14. When actions or annual rents, or servitudes and rights, fall under the names of movables or immovables, Gabriel explains in Commentarii opinionum, book 6, On the meaning of words, conclusions 7 and 8.

units.la: Et quænam mobilibus vel immobilibus sint annumeranda? Determinant varii: ut Tiraquell.de jure Primogen. q.47.48.49.usque ad p. 64.versum Chassan.ad Burgund.Rubric. 10.§. 1. verb. son heritage n.8.Argentr.ad Brittann.artic. 60.Gloss. 3. n. 7. Ann. Robert.3.Judic.9. Francisc. Sarmient 6. select. interpr. 15. Chopin.de Moribus Paris. libr. 1. tit. 1. per totum. Johan. le Cerier. de Primogen. q. 6. 7. 8. 9. libr. 2. Montan. de Tutel. c. 33.n. 123. Barbos. collect. in Cod. ad l. 14. n. 5. 8. Cod. Sacros. Eccles. Thesaur. decis. 160. Cujac. Parat. Cod. in quibus caus. cessat, long. tempor. præscr. & ad tit. 2. libr.1. feud. Goris ad consuet. Vestlav. c. 13. art. 4. gloss. 1. p. 210. & c.14. p. 213. Zoes. D.Rer. divis.n. 5.6. & D. Adq. Domin. n. 74. Herbajus. Rer. quot. c. 18. Mev. ad Lubec. part. 1. qu. 6. n. 25. & libr. 1. tit. 10. art. 6. n. 70. Anton. Matth. disp. 2. de Servit. n. 6.
units.tr: And which things are to be counted among movables or immovables? Various authors determine this: as Tiraquellus, On the Right of Primogeniture, questions 47, 48, 49, up to p. 64; the verse Chassanaeus on the Burgundy rubric 10, §1, word "son héritage", n. 8; Argentré on the Brittany article 60, gloss 3, n. 7; Annus Robertus, 3 Judicia 9; Franciscus Sarmiento, 6 Select Interpretations 15; Chopinus, On the Customs of Paris, book 1, title 1, throughout; Johannes le Cerier, On Primogeniture, questions 6–9, book 2; Montanus, On Guardianship, chapter 33, n. 123; Barbosa, collected notes on the Code, on l. 14, n. 5, 8; Cod. Sacros. Eccles. Thesaurus, decision 160; Cujacius, Paratitla on the Code, In quibus causis cessat longi temporis praescriptio, and on title 2, book 1 of the Feudal Law; Goris on the Customs of Westvlaanderen, chapter 13, art. 4, gloss 1, p. 210, and chapter 14, p. 213; Zoesius, De rerum divisione, n. 5, 6, and De adquirendo dominio, n. 74; Herbajus, De rebus quotidianis, chapter 18; Meves on Lübeck, part 1, question 6, n. 25, and book 1, title 10, art. 6, n. 70; Antonius Matthaeus, Disputation 2 On Servitudes, n. 6.

units.la: SECT. IX. CAP. II.
units.tr: Section IX, Chapter II.

units.la: 1. Quid si quis testetur in loco domicilii, adhibitis solemnibus loci, ubi res sita?
units.tr: 1. What if someone makes a will at his domicile, using the solemnities of the place where the property is situated?

units.la: 2. Quid si quis testetur secundum sui loci solemnia?
units.tr: 2. What if someone makes a will according to the solemnities of his own place?

units.la: 3. Quid si forensis secundum loci statutum testamentum condat, ubi tantum hospitatur? 0 2 4. Quid
units.tr: 3. What if a stranger makes a will according to the statute of a place where he merely lodges? 4. What

units.la: 4. Quid si in fraudem statuti alibi testamentum condat?
units.tr: 4. What if someone makes a will elsewhere in fraud of a statute?

units.la: 5. Quid si forensis cum virgine matrimonium ineat, an contrahere censebitur secundum statutum patriæ virginis?
units.tr: 5. What if a foreigner contracts marriage with a virgin: will he be deemed to contract according to the statute of the virgin's homeland?

units.la: 6. Quid si de lucro dotis contentio, cujus loci spectandum erit statutum?
units.tr: 6. What if a dispute arises over the gain from a dowry: which place's statute is to be looked to?

units.la: 7. Quid si maritus domicilium transtulerit, an prioris an posterioris spectandum erit statutum?
units.tr: 7. What if a husband has transferred his domicile: is the statute of the former domicile or of the later one to be looked to?

units.la: 8. Quid si statutum loquatur de hypothecâ, competenti uxori in mariti bonis?
units.tr: 8. What if the statute speaks of a mortgage granted to a wife over her husband's goods?

units.la: 9. Quid si de contractibus proprie dictis eorumque solemnibus contentio? Ubi & variæ exceptiones.
units.tr: 9. What if there is a dispute about contracts properly so called and their solemnities? Here also there are various exceptions.

units.la: 10. Quid si de contractus naturâ, deque iis, quæ eum comitantur, sit contentio?
units.tr: 10. What if there is a dispute about the nature of a contract and about the things that accompany it?

units.la: 11. Quotuplex sit locus contractus?
units.tr: 11. How many kinds of place of contract are there?

units.la: 12. Quis locus spectandus in ratione effectus seu complementi contractus?
units.tr: 12. Which place is to be looked to in respect of the effect or completion of a contract?

units.la: 13. Quid si alternative in plura loca destinata sit solutio?
units.tr: 13. What if payment is designated alternatively in several places?

units.la: 14. Quid si de litteris cambii incidat quæstio? 15. Quid
units.tr: 14. What if a question arises about bills of exchange? 15. What

units.la: 15. Quid si de valore nummorum contentio?
units.tr: 15. What if there is a dispute about the value of money?

units.la: 16. Quid si credita sint 10. dolia vini Aurelianensis, Amsterodami solvenda?
units.tr: 16. What if ten casks of Orléans wine were lent, to be paid back at Amsterdam?

units.la: 17. Quid si pupillo dandus sit tutor?
units.tr: 17. What if a guardian must be given to a ward?

units.la: 18. Quid si curator bonis dandus?
units.tr: 18. What if a curator must be given to the property?

units.la: 19. Quid si rationes sint reddendae?
units.tr: 19. What if accounts must be rendered?

units.la: 20. In integrum restitutione petita, quale statutum spectandum?
units.tr: 20. When restitution in integrum is sought, which statute is to be looked to?

units.la: 21. Quid si mulier adversus dotem velit restitui?
units.tr: 21. What if a woman wishes to be restored against her dowry?

units.la: 1. VErum, quid de Solemnibus, in negotiis, adhibendis, statuendum erit si locorum statuta discrepent? Finge quempiam testari in loco domicilii adhibitis solemnibus rei sitae, non sui domicilii, valebit ne testamentum ratione bonorum alibi sitorum? Resp. quod non. Neque enim aliter testamentum valere potest, quam si ea servetur solemnitas, quam requirit locus gestionis. Argum. l. sin. Cod. Testam. l. 1. Cod. Emanc. Gudelinus de jure novissl. libr. 2. c. 5. Perez. Cod. de Testam. n. 21, vid. Mev. quest. Pralim. 6. n 8. ibique alii. Rodenb. de jure conj. c. 3 tit. 2. n. 2. & c. 4. tit, 2. n. 4.
units.tr: 1. But what is to be decided about the solemnities to be observed in transactions, if the statutes of the places disagree? Suppose someone makes a will at his domicile, using the solemnities of the place where the property lies, not of his own domicile: will the will be valid with regard to goods situated elsewhere? Answer: no. For a will cannot be valid unless the solemnity which the place of the transaction requires is observed. Argument: l. sin. Cod. Testam.; l. 1. Cod. Emanc.; Gudelinus, De jure novissimo, lib. 2, c. 5; Perez, Cod. de Testam. n. 21; see Mev., quaest. praelim. 6, n. 8, and the others cited there; Rodenb., De jure conj., c. 3, tit. 2, n. 2, and c. 4, tit. 2, n. 4.

units.la: 2. Quid si quispiam testetur secundum solemnia sui loci, puta coram notario & duobus bus testibus, an vires capiet testamentum ratione bonorum, extra territorium statuentis jacentium, puta in Frisia, ubi plures solemnitates requiruntur? Aff. Idque procedit sive testator domicilium prius retinuerit, sive alio transtulerit. Arg. l. fin. Cod. Testam. l. fin. D. Testam. Milit. l. 27. Cod. Donat. Gail. 2. obs. 123. Mynsing. 5. Observ. 20. Salicet. Cod. summ. Trinit. l. 1. n. 8. in fin. Gabriel. comm. opin. libr. 6. de Consuet. concl. 2, ibique varii, cum limitationibus. Baptista Villalobos in tom. comm. opin. verb statutum. p. 354. Johannes Bertachin, de Episcop. libr. 4. part. 2. quaest. 18. n. 45. Peck. de Testam. conjug. libr. 4. c. 28. n. 9. units.tr: 2. What if someone makes a will according to the solemnities of his own place, for example before a notary and two witnesses: will the will take effect with regard to goods lying outside the territory of the one who made the statute, for example in Friesland, where more solemnities are required? Yes. And this holds whether the testator has kept his earlier domicile or has transferred it elsewhere. Arg. l. fin. Cod. Testam.; l. fin. D. Testam. Milit.; l. 27. Cod. Donat.; Gail, 2 obs. 123; Mynsing, 5 Observ. 20; Salicet., Cod. summ. units.la: 3. Quid si forensis secundum loci statutum testamentum condat, ubi tantum hospitatur, an valebit alibi, ubi vel immobilia, vel domicilium habet? Respondeo, quod ita. Cum enim hic agatur de actus solemnitate, quae quocunque obligat in loco negotium aliquod gerentes, etiam obligabit forensem ibi disponentem, si suam dispositionem, vel suum actum velit utilem; licet non praecise liget eundem. Statutum quippe circa solemnia nec est in rem, nec in personam, sed mixti generis: quod etiam obligare forensem ibi, ubi quid gerit, in capite de statutorum divisione fuit explicatum. Nisi tamen privilegii loco aliquid datum sit civibus, exclusis extraneis. Arg. l. 7. D. de Reg. jur. l. ult. D. Testam. Milit. l. ult. Cod. de Testam. Bartol. in l. 1. Cod. Emanc. liberor. Alexand. consil. 44. vol. 5. Gail. 2. obs. 123. Boër. ad Bituric. tit. 8. §. 4. p. 119. post Bartol. Baldum. aliosque. Sichard. in l. 9. Cod. de Testam. n. 10. Bocer. classe 1. disp. 3. n. 43. diff. Oldrad. consil. 248. Cujac. 14. obs. 12. Burgund. ad Consuet. Flandr. tract. 6. Befold. ad l. 9. tit. 1. libr. 1. D. n. 5. 6. Gothefr. ad l. ult. D. de Jurisd. Gilken. ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit, n. 60.
units.tr: 3. What if a stranger makes a will according to the statute of the place where he merely lodges: will it be valid in another place, where he has immovable property or a domicile? I answer that it will. For since we are here dealing with the solemnity of an act, which binds all who transact some business in a place, it will also bind the stranger who disposes there, if he wishes his disposition or his act to be effective, although it does not strictly bind him personally. For a statute concerning solemnities is neither real nor personal but of a mixed kind; and that it binds the stranger where he acts was explained in the chapter on the division of statutes. Unless, however, something has been granted to citizens as a privilege, excluding outsiders. Arg. l. 7. D. de Reg. jur.; l. ult. D. Testam. Milit.; l. ult. Cod. de Testam.; Bartol., in l. 1. Cod. Emanc. liberor.; Alexand., consil. 44, vol. 5; Gail, 2 obs. 123; Boër, ad Bituric., tit. 8, §. 4, p. 119, after Bartolus, Baldus and others; Sichard, in l. 9. Cod. de Testam., n. 10; Bocer, classis 1, disp. 3, n. 43, contra; Oldrad., consil. 248; Cujac., 14 obs. 12; Burgund., ad Consuet. Flandr., tract. 6; Befold, ad l. 9, tit. 1, lib. 1 D., n. 5, 6; Gothofr., ad l. ult. D. de Jurisd.; Gilken, ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit., n. 60.

units.la: 4. Si tamen quispiam, ut evitaret solemnitatem loci sui domicilii, in fraudem talis statuti extra territorium se conferat, ejus testamentum non valere, existumarem. Aretin. Bald. & alii apud Gabriel. Commun. Opin. libr. 6. de Statut. conclus. 8. n. 21 22.
units.tr: 4. If, however, someone, in order to avoid the solemnity required by the statute of his own domicile, betakes himself outside its territory in fraud of such a statute, I would judge that his will is not valid. Aretin., Bald. and others, cited in Gabriel, Commun. Opin., lib. 6, de Statut., concl. 8, n. 21, 22.

units.la: 5. Verum ad pacta & contractus memet conferam, Ubi principio inquirendum, de pacto seu contractu nuptiali, an si forensis matrimonium ineat cum virgine non suae civitatis, contrahere censeatur, secundum suae patriae statuta, an domicilii virginis?
units.tr: 5. But I shall now turn to pacts and contracts. Here we must first inquire about the pact or contract of marriage: if a foreigner contracts marriage with a virgin who is not of his own city, is he deemed to contract according to the statutes of his own homeland, or according to those of the virgin's domicile?

units.la: O 4. ResponRespondeo, quia mulier quæ in matrimonii leges consensit, judicatur respicere domicilium mariti, in quod deducenda; & non simpliciter dicitur quis esse in loco, in quo corporaliter consistit, sed in què fertur animi destinatione, quomodo & domicilium mutari dicitur. Potius secundum illius domicilii leges censebitur contraxisse, quam secundum leges loci ubi ipsa viro jungitur & domicilium habet. Nisi tamen maritus in domicilio uxoris contrahat animo ibidem commorandi, quo casu forte pro naturali cive censendus. Vel nisi expresse pactis antenuptialibus aliter fuerit conventum. l. nihil. 2. D. Captiv. l. 65. D. de judic. ubi Costal. Argum. l. 35. §. 3. D. hared. instit. l. 32. in sin. D. de Pignor. & Hypoth. l. 1. §. 32. D. depos. DD. varii apud Lambert. Goris Advs juris part. 1. c. 6. n. 3. & seq. Barbos. ad l. 19. §. proinde. in artic. de foro Origin. D. judic. n. 9. 10. 11. & §. sin. d. l. 19. n. 70. & seqq. & ad l. 65. D. judic. ubi varie limitationes.
units.tr: 4. I answer: because a woman who has consented to the laws of marriage is judged to look to the domicile of her husband, into which she is to be brought; and a person is not said to be in the place where he is bodily present merely, but in the place towards which his mind is directed, just as a domicile is said to be changed in this way. He will rather be deemed to have contracted according to the laws of that domicile than according to the laws of the place where the woman is joined to the man and has her domicile. Unless, however, the husband contracts in the wife's domicile with the intention of living there, in which case he may perhaps be deemed a native citizen; or unless it has been expressly agreed otherwise by antenuptial pacts. l. nihil. 2. D. Captiv.; l. 65. D. de judic., where Costalius; Argument, l. 35. §. 3. D. hered. instit.; l. 32. in fin. D. de Pignor. et Hypoth.; l. 1. §. 32. D. depos.; various jurists cited in Lambert Goris, Advocatus juris, part. 1, c. 6, n. 3 et seq.; Barbos., ad l. 19. §. proinde, in articulo de foro originis, D. judic., n. 9, 10, 11, and §. sin., d. l. 19, n. 70 et seqq., and ad l. 65. D. judic., with various limitations.

units.la: 6. Quid si contentio de lucro dotis incidat, an spectandum erit statutum loci contracti matrimonii, si quidem ibidem pacta nuptialia concepta, an domicilii mariti? Respondeo, & si forte prima fronte videretur dicendum inspici oportere locum contractus, quod ei sese videantur subjecisse contrahentes: quia tamen in casu proposito, non tam agitur de ipso contractu, quam contractus executione, seu de loco, ad quem respexere contrahen-tes, is autem sit locus domicilii mariti, cui se se mulier subjecit; etiam statutum domicilii mariti respici debebit.
units.tr: 6. What if a dispute arises over the gain from a dowry: is the statute of the place where the marriage was contracted to be looked to, since the antenuptial pacts were drawn up there, or the statute of the husband's domicile? I answer: although at first sight it might seem that the place of the contract must be examined, because the contracting parties appear to have submitted themselves to it, nevertheless, since in the case proposed the question concerns not so much the contract itself as its execution, that is, the place to which the contracting parties looked, and that place is the domicile of the husband, to which the woman has submitted herself, the statute of the husband's domicile must also be regarded.

units.la: Idem quod dicendum, si marito, vel uxore prædefuncta, inter superstitem & hæredes defuncti, bonorum divisio sit instituen-da. l. 65. D. judic. l. contraxisse. D. Oblig. Action. ibidemque Gloss. fin. l. ult. Cod. de incol. l. 1. Cod. de Mulier. & in quo loc. Alexand. vol. 1. libr. 3. conf. 100. n. 8. Covarr. de Matrim. p. 2. c. 7. in princ. n. 5. & seq. Campeg. de dote p. 5. q. 20. n. 3. ibique alii. Mynsi. 4. obs. 82. Surd. decis. 226. Vivius in tom. comm. opinion. libr. 17. verb. Statutum op. 341. Everhard. consil. 78. Gomes. ad l. Zauri. 50. n. 75. ubi habet aliquot limitat. Garc. de acquest. Conjug. n. 140. & seqq. vid. & Argentr. ad Brittann. artic. 218. gloss. 6. n. 33. & seqq. & potissimum n. 45. ibique DD. Zoes. D. de Pact. Dotalibus. n. 14. Perez. Cod. Rei Uxor. Action. n 16. Barbos. ad l. 65. D. judic. Ut tamen Jason. in l. 1. Cod. de Summ. Trinit. n. 24. illam communem opinionem in septem casibus limitet. Bartol. Purpurat. Gilken. prolixe in d. l. 1. Cod. init. & n. 27. & seqq. ex prof. Roland. à Valle de lucro dot. vid. Andr. ab Exea. in c. agnoscentes. de Constit. tom. 2. p. 254. n. 45. & Vincent. Caroc. in c. cum quid. de Reg. jur. in 6. p. 2. limit. 6. Tom. 5. p. 980. & q. 1. n. 10. p. 962. in Re-perti jur. canon.
units.tr: The same must be said if, on the death of one spouse, a division of the goods has to be made between the survivor and the heirs of the deceased. l. 65. D. judic. l. contraxisse. D. Oblig. Action. and the Gloss there, fin. l. ult. Cod. de incol. l. 1. Cod. de Mulier. & in quo loc. Alexand. vol. 1. libr. 3. conf. 100. n. 8. Covarr. de Matrim. p. 2. c. 7. in princ. n. 5. & seq. Campeg. de dote p. 5. q. 20. n. 3. and the others there. Mynsi. 4. obs. 82. Surd. decis. 226. Vivius in tom. comm. opinion. libr. 17. verb. Statutum op. 341. Everhard. consil. 78. Gomes. ad l. Zauri. 50. n. 75, where he gives several limitations. Garc. de acquest. Conjug. n. 140. & seqq. See also Argentr. ad Brittann. artic. 218. gloss. 6. n. 33. & seqq., and especially n. 45 and the DD. there. Zoes. D. de Pact. Dotalibus. n. 14. Perez. Cod. Rei Uxor. Action. n. 16. Barbos. ad l. 65. D. judic. Yet Jason, in l. 1. Cod. de Summ. Trinit. n. 24, limits that common opinion in seven cases. Bartol. Purpurat. Gilken. at length in the said l. 1. Cod. init., and n. 27. & seqq. From Roland. à Valle on the profit of dowry, see Andr. ab Exea. in c. agnoscentes. de Constit. tom. 2. p. 254. n. 45, and Vincent. Caroc. in c. cum quid. de Reg. jur. in 6. p. 2. limit. 6. Tom. 5. p. 980, and q. 1. n. 10. p. 962, in Repert. jur. canon.

units.la: 7. Quid si maritus alio domicilium postmodum transtulerit, eritne conveniendus, secundum loci statutum, in quem postremum sese recepit? Non equidem. Quia non eo ipso, quod domicilium transferat, censetur voluntatem circa pacta nuptialia mutasse. Argum. D. l. 22. D. Prob. Nisi eadem solemnitas in actu contrario intercesserit, Arg. l. 35. D. Reg. jur. Gilken. ad init. tit. Cod. Sum. Trinit. n. 32. & seqq. Accedit, quod illa pacta solus mutare nequeat maritus: id quod tamen posset, si per emigrationem in alium locum, ea mutarentur. Est quippe in ejus solius potestate, invita uxore, alio sese conferre. l. 4. §. Proficisci. D. Off. Proconf. l. 22. §. si maritus. D. Solut. Matrim. Ne dicam, spectari non debere in pactis antenuptialibus, incertum migrationis eventum; adeoque nec ab eventu incerto ipsa dependere, de quo per contrahentes ne quidem fuit cogitatum. l. 9. §. sin. D. Transf.
units.tr: 7. What if the husband afterwards transfers his domicile to another place: will he be sued according to the statute of the place to which he last removed? Certainly not. Because by the mere fact that he transfers his domicile, he is not held to have changed his intention concerning the marriage agreements. Argum. D. l. 22. D. Prob. Unless the same solemnity has attended the contrary act. Arg. l. 35. D. Reg. jur. Gilken. ad init. tit. Cod. Sum. Trinit. n. 32. & seqq. Moreover, the husband alone cannot change those agreements; yet he could do so if they were changed by emigration to another place. For it lies in his power alone, against his wife's will, to betake himself elsewhere. l. 4. §. Proficisci. D. Off. Proconf. l. 22. §. si maritus. D. Solut. Matrim. Not to mention that in antenuptial agreements the uncertain outcome of a migration ought not to be considered, and so the agreement cannot depend upon an uncertain event which the contracting parties never even thought of. l. 9. §. sin. D. Transf.

units.la: 8. Quid si statutum loquatur de hypotheca in mariti bonis uxori competenti; spectabiturne locus domicilii mariti, an contracti matrimonii, an rei sitae? Respondeo, quia Bona mobilia sequuntur domicilium debitoris, quod ibidem esse intelligantur, quoad illa spectabitur, locus habitationis mariti. Quia vero immobilia reguntur locorum statutis, ubi sita; etiam quoad ea, si de aestimanda hypotheca, aut de privilegiis inter hypothecarios agatur, non inspiciendus erit locus domicilii, vel debitoris, vel creditoris, verum locus statuti, ubi jacent per l. ult. D. jurisd. Burgund. ad Consuet. Flandr. tract. 1. n. 6. 7. Campeg. de dote. Septim. vol. Tract. Argentr. ad Brittan. artic. 218. n. 45. Sanden de feud. Gelr. tract. 1. tit. 3. c. 2. n. 4. Anton. Matth. de Auctione. libr. 1. c. 21. n. 35. & seq. & num. 41. Rodenb. de jure conjug. tit. 2. c. 5. n. 16. Des-sel. in not. ad Zoes. institut. de Testam. ordin. n. 16.
units.tr: 8. What if the statute speaks of a mortgage on the husband's goods in favour of the wife: will the place of the husband's domicile be regarded, or the place of the marriage contract, or the place where the property lies? I answer: since movable goods follow the domicile of the debtor, which is understood to be where he lives, the place of the husband's residence will be looked to as regards those. But since immovable goods are governed by the statutes of the place where they lie, so too as regards them, if the value of the mortgage or the priority among mortgage creditors is in question, the place of domicile of either debtor or creditor is not to be examined, but the place of the statute where the property lies. per l. ult. D. jurisd. Burgund. ad Consuet. Flandr. tract. 1. n. 6. 7. Campeg. de dote. Septim. vol. Tract. Argentr. ad Brittan. artic. 218. n. 45. Sanden de feud. Gelr. tract. 1. tit. 3. c. 2. n. 4. Anton. Matth. de Auctione. libr. 1. c. 21. n. 35. & seq. & num. 41. Rodenb. de jure conjug. tit. 2. c. 5. n. 16. Dessel. in not. ad Zoes. institut. de Testam. ordin. n. 16.

units.la: 9. Quid si de contractubus proprie dic-tis, & quidem eorum solemnibus contentio; quis locus spectabitur; an domicilii contrahentis, an loci, ubi quis contrahit? Resp. Aff. Posterius. Quia censetur quis semet contrahendo, legibus istius loci, ubi contrahit, etiam ratione solemnium subjicere voluisse. Ut quemadmodum loci consuetudo subintrat contractum, cujusque est declarativa, ita etiam loci statutum. l. 31. §. 20. D. Ædil. Edict. l. 1. Cod. Emancip. liber. l. 32. D. de leg. l. semper 34. D. Reg. jur. l. 818. D. locat. Bartol. ad l. 1. Cod. summ. Trinit. n. 13. Bald. n. 93. Salicet. Cod. eod. n. 8. in fin. Alexand. vol. 3. consil. 100. n. 15. Cravett. consil. 271. Chassan, ad consuet. Burgund. Rubric. 4. §. 2. verb. secundum generalem consuet. n. 1. & seq. Barbos. ad l. hæres absens. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 74. & ad l. 65.
units.tr: 9. What if the dispute concerns contracts properly so called, and especially their solemn forms? Which place is to be considered: the domicile of the contracting party, or the place where he contracts? Answer: the affirmative, the latter. For a person is deemed, by contracting, to have wished to submit himself to the laws of the place where he contracts, including as regards the solemn forms. Just as the custom of a place enters into a contract and declares its nature, so too does the statute of the place. Dig. Ædil. Edict. l. 31 §20; Cod. Emancip. liber. l. 1; Dig. de leg. l. 32; Dig. Reg. jur. l. semper 34; Dig. locat. l. 818; Bartolus on Cod. summ. Trinit. l. 1 n. 13; Baldus n. 93; Salicetus, Cod. eod. n. 8 in fin.; Alexander, vol. 3 consil. 100 n. 15; Cravetta consil. 271; Chassanaeus on the custom of Burgundy, rubric 4 §2, verb. secundum generalem consuetudinem n. 1 et seq.; Barbosa on l. hæres absens §proinde, Dig. judic. n. 74, and on l. 65.

units.la: O eod. n. 104. Anton. Matth. de Auction. libr. I. c. 21. n. 37.
units.tr: Ibid. n. 104. Anton. Matth. de Auction. libr. I. c. 21. n. 37.

units.la: Excipe 1. Si Princeps alibi contrahat, ut qui juris solemnibus est solutus. §. sin. in sin. instit. injust. Rupt. irrit. testam. l. 31. D. de leg. Post Roman. consil. 444. n. 10. Menoch. 3. Præs. 44. n. 19. Roel. à Valle de lucro dot. q. 84. n. 7. Mascard. de interpret. statut. concl. 7. n. 49.
units.tr: Make an exception: (1) if the Prince contracts elsewhere, since he is released from the solemn forms of the law (§ sin. in fin. Instit. de injust.; Rupt. irrit. testam.; Dig. de leg. l. 31); Post, Romanus consil. 444 n. 10; Menochius 3 Praes. 44 n. 19; Roel à Valle de lucro dot. q. 84 n. 7; Mascardus de interpret. statut. concl. 7 n. 49.

units.la: Neque enim Princeps statuto à se approbato ligatur. Bartol. in l. Lucius Titius. §. 2. D. fideic. libert. ego in cap. de Effect. statutor. Nisi tamen sponte semet loci solemnibus subjicere voluerit. Arg. §. sin. & l. 4. Cod. de leg. Menoch. 2. Præs. 5. n. 2.
units.tr: For a Prince is not bound by a statute which he himself has approved. Bartol. in l. Lucius Titius. §. 2. D. fideic. libert. ego in cap. de Effect. statutor. Unless, however, he has of his own accord chosen to submit himself to the solemnities of that place. Arg. §. sin. & l. 4. Cod. de leg. Menoch. 2. Præs. 5. n. 2.

units.la: Excipe. 2. Si contractus coram Principe fuerit celebratus, aut forte in gratiam Principis. Ratio prioris est, quia suâ præsentiâ supplet omnes juris solemnitates. l. 19. in invit. Cod. de Testam. Ratio posterioris est, favor & Privilegium Principis. Sic enim Principi donatio facta non eget insinuatione licet quingentos aureos excesserit. Nov. 52. c. 2.
units.tr: Exception 2. If the contract was celebrated before the Prince, or perhaps for the sake of the Prince's favour. The reason for the former is that by his presence he supplies all the solemnities of law. l. 19. in invit. Cod. de Testam. The reason for the latter is the favour and privilege of the Prince. Thus a gift made to a Prince does not need insinuation, even if it exceeds five hundred gold pieces. Nov. 52. c. 2.

units.la: Excipe 3. Nisi quis, quo in loco domicilii evitaret molestam aliquam vel sumptuosam solemnitatem, adeoque in fraudem sui statuti nullâ necessitate cogente alio proficiscatur, & mox ad locum domicilii, gesto alibi negotio, revertatur. Mascard. d. tract. concl. 6. n. 134. post Aretin. conf. 54.
units.tr: Exception 3. Unless someone, in order to avoid some troublesome or costly solemnity at the place of his domicile, and so in fraud of his own statute, and with no compelling necessity, goes elsewhere and soon returns to the place of his domicile, having transacted business elsewhere. Mascard. d. tract. concl. 6. n. 134. post Aretin. conf. 54.

units.la: Excipe 4. Nisi etiam extra locum domicilii velit uti statuto suæ patriæ favorabili, quoad solemnia; tu forte contractus alibi itagestus, ubi alia solemnia erant adhibenda, ex æquo & bono in patria, sustineretur. Bartol. in l. imperatores §. idem rescripserunt. D. Ad Munic. Masc d. tract. concl. 6 n. 114. Atque hæc eadem, quæ de contractibus dicta, etiam testamentorum solemnibus applicari poterunt: excepto responso secundo exceptionis secundæ per §. sin. Instit. de injust. Rupt. irrito. vid. Jason. vol. 1. consil. 48. Matth. Gribald. in tom. comm. opin. libr. 17. verb. statutum. p. 332. Gilken. ad init. Cod. summ. Trinit. n. 15. 16. Gail, 2. obs. 123. Mynsi. 4. obs. 82.
units.tr: Exception 4. Unless one also wishes, outside the place of domicile, to use the statute of one's own homeland, which is favourable as regards solemnities; so that a contract made elsewhere, where other solemnities had to be observed, would be upheld in one's homeland by equity and good conscience. Bartol. in l. imperatores §. idem rescripserunt. D. Ad Munic. Masc d. tract. concl. 6 n. 114. And what has been said of contracts may also be applied to the solemnities of wills, except the second answer to the second exception, by reason of §. sin. Instit. de injust. Rupt. irrito. vid. Jason. vol. 1. consil. 48. Matth. Gribald. in tom. comm. opin. libr. 17. verb. statutum. p. 332. Gilken. ad init. Cod. summ. Trinit. n. 15. 16. Gail, 2. obs. 123. Mynsi. 4. obs. 82.

units.la: 10. Quod si de ipso contractu quæratur, seu de natura ipsius contractus, seu iis quæ ex natura contractus veniunt, puta fidejussione &c. etiam spectandum est loci statutum, ubi contractus celebratur, per ll. anteriores: quod ei contrahentes semet accommodare præsumantur. addet. 6. D. de Evict. Bartol. loc. cit. n. 16. Alexand. vol. 2. consil. 37. col. 2. & column. 4, ad sin. Surd. decis. 13. n. 6. Chassan. ad Burg. rubr. 4. §. 2. verb. cit. Merul. Prax. civil. libr. 4. dist. 4. sect. 3. tit. 4. c. 3. n. 17. Mevium ad Lubecens. quæst. Præl. 4. n. 10.
units.tr: 10. But if the question concerns the contract itself, whether its nature or what arises from the nature of the contract, such as suretyship etc., the statute of the place where the contract is made is also to be regarded, by the earlier laws, because the contracting parties are presumed to have accommodated themselves to it. addet. 6. D. de Evict. Bartol. loc. cit. n. 16. Alexand. vol. 2. consil. 37. col. 2. & column. 4, ad sin. Surd. decis. 13. n. 6. Chassan. ad Burg. rubr. 4. §. 2. verb. cit. Merul. Prax. civil. libr. 4. dist. 4. sect. 3. tit. 4. c. 3. n. 17. Mevium ad Lubecens. quæst. Præl. 4. n. 10.

units.la: Nisi tamen cum aliquo contrahens, sciat cum statim recessurum esse, quo casu talem conveniri in loco contractus non oportet, nisi pro his quae statim quis tradere tenetur. Aut nisi expresse promisit se ibi soluturum. Post Alex. conf. 89. n. 1. libr. 7. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 94. ibique plures, & n. 114. n. 134. 135. Aut nisi etiam quis reipublicae causa transit per locum contractus, ut si fit legatus; quo casu nec in loco contractus convenietur. d. loc. n. 136.
units.tr: Unless, however, a person contracting with someone knows that the other will depart at once, in which case he need not be sued at the place of contract, except for those things which he is bound to hand over immediately. Or unless he has expressly promised to pay there. After Alex. conf. 89. n. 1. libr. 7. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 94. ibique plures, & n. 114. n. 134. 135. Or unless someone passes through the place of contract on public business, as when he becomes an envoy; in which case he also cannot be sued at the place of contract. d. loc. n. 136.

units.la: Id quod etiam referri poterit ad onera contractuum, puta gabellas, & similia solvenda in loco, ubi gestum est negotium, licet res vendita alibi sita. Bald. l. 1. n. 3. Cod. Contr. Empt. & alii multi apud Barbof. ad l. 19. §. proinde D. de Judic. n. 77. & seqq.
units.tr: This can also be referred to the burdens of contracts, for example tolls and similar charges, which are to be paid in the place where the business was transacted, even though the thing sold is situated elsewhere. Bald. l. 1. n. 3. Cod. Contr. Empt. & alii multi apud Barbof. ad l. 19. §. proinde D. de Judic. n. 77. & seqq.

units.la: Nisi expresso statuto cautum sit ut gabellae in loco traditionis vel consummationis contractus sint solvendae. Barbof. d. l. n. 84. & seqq.
units.tr: Unless an express statute provides that tolls are to be paid in the place of delivery or completion of the contract. Barbof. d. l. n. 84. & seqq.

units.la: Vel nisi distincta sint territoria, quae uni Principi non parent.
units.tr: Or unless the territories are distinct and do not obey one Prince.

units.la: 11. Ne tamen hic oriatur confusio, locum contractus duplicem facio, alium, ubi fit, de quo jam dictum, alium in quem destinata solutio. Illum locum verum, hunc fictum appellat Salicet. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 4. Uterque tamen recte locus dicitur contractus, etiam secundum leges civiles, licet postremus aliquid fictionis contineat. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. sin. n. 6. 16. D. judic.
units.tr: 11. Lest confusion arise here, I distinguish a twofold place of contract: one where it is made, of which I have already spoken, and another to which payment is destined. Salicet. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 4. calls the former the true place and the latter the fictitious place. Yet both are rightly called the place of the contract, even according to the civil laws, although the latter contains some element of fiction. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. sin. n. 6. 16. D. judic.

units.la: 12. Hinc ratione effectus, & complementi ipsius contractus, spectatur ille locus, inquem destinata est solutio; id quod ad modum, mensuram, usuras, &c. negligentiam & moram post contractum initum accedentem, referendum est. l. 21. D. oblig. Action. ibique Gothefr. l. 1. in Princ. D. de Usur. ibique Gloss. l. 1. 2. 3. D. Rebus auct. judic.poss. l. 8. 18. 19. Cod. locat. l. 22. D. de Rebus credit. l, Semper in stipulat. D. Reg. jur. l. in hac. D. Tritic. action. l. 65. D. de judic. In qua lege, meo judicio, nihil speciale. Bartol. Purpur. Salic. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. Gilken. ibidem, n. 22. 28, 29. Mascard. tract. all. concl. 7. n. 75. vid. Barbos. prolixe in l. hares absens. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 57. & seqq. & n. 63. & seqq. & §. sin. ibid. n. 9, 10. 11. 12. & seqq. & ad l. 65. eod. n. 105.
units.tr: 12. Hence, with regard to the effect and completion of the contract itself, that place is regarded to which payment is destined; and this is to be referred to the mode, the measure, the interest, and so on, and to negligence and delay arising after the contract has been entered into. l. 21. D. oblig. Action. ibique Gothefr. l. 1. in Princ. D. de Usur. ibique Gloss. l. 1. 2. 3. D. Rebus auct. judic.poss. l. 8. 18. 19. Cod. locat. l. 22. D. de Rebus credit. l, Semper in stipulat. D. Reg. jur. l. in hac. D. Tritic. action. l. 65. D. de judic. In that law, in my judgment, there is nothing special. Bartol. Purpur. Salic. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. Gilken. ibidem, n. 22. 28, 29. Mascard. tract. all. concl. 7. n. 75. see Barbos. at length in l. hares absens. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 57. & seqq. & n. 63. & seqq. & §. sin. ibid. n. 9, 10. 11. 12. & seqq. & ad l. 65. eod. n. 105.

units.la: 13. Quid si alternative in plura loca destinata sit solutio, sic ut electio sit actoris? Spectabitur statutum loci ubi quid petitur, si modo vel ibi reperiatur debitor, vel habeat ibidem domicilium. l. 4. D. Condict. Tritic. l. 2. §. 3. D quod certo loco. l. 22. D. Rebus credit. c. sin. de haeret. Bartol. loc. alleg. n. 18. Salicet. ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 5.
units.tr: 13. What if payment is destined alternatively for several places, so that the choice lies with the plaintiff? The statute of the place where the claim is made will be regarded, provided the debtor is found there or has a domicile there. l. 4. D. Condict. Tritic. l. 2. §. 3. D quod certo loco. l. 22. D. Rebus credit. c. sin. de haeret. Bartol. loc. alleg. n. 18. Salicet. ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 5.

units.la: 14. Quid si de litteris cambii incidat quaestio, quis locus erit spectandus? Is spectandus est locus, ad quem sunt destinatae, & ibidem acceptatae. Argum. l. qui autem. in sin. D. Constit. Pecun. gloss. in l. 1. verb. & per litteras. litteras, D. Contrah. Empt. Masc. tract. all. conclus. 7. n. 72.
units.tr: 14. What if a question arises concerning bills of exchange: which place is to be regarded? The place is to be regarded to which they are directed, and where they have been accepted. Argum. l. qui autem. in sin. D. Constit. Pecun. gloss. in l. 1. verb. & per litteras. litteras, D. Contrah. Empt. Masc. tract. all. conclus. 7. n. 72.

units.la: 15. Quid si in specie, de nummorum aut reditu um solutione difficultas incidat, si forte valor sit immutatus, an spectabitur loci valor, ubi contractus erat celebratus, an loci, in quem destinata erat solutio? Respondeo, ex generali regula, spectandum esse loci statutum, in quem destinata erat solutio. per d. l. 22. in fin. D. Rebus credit. l. 3. in fin. D. Rebus auct. jud. Poss. l. fin. D. Tritic. Action. l. 3. §. 3. D. Action. Empt. Bald. Angel. in l. fi fundus. D. Evict. & Bald. in l. quaero. D. Solut. & in Auth. quas actiones Cod. Sacrof. Eccles. Nicol. Everhard. consil. 78. post Cyn. Albericum, de Rosat. Alex. immol. Jason. n. 9. 10.
units.tr: 15. What if, in a particular case, a difficulty arises concerning the payment of money or income, namely whether, if the value has perhaps changed, the value of the place where the contract was made is to be regarded, or the value of the place to which payment was destined? I answer that, by the general rule, the statute of the place to which payment was destined is to be regarded. per d. l. 22. in fin. D. Rebus credit. l. 3. in fin. D. Rebus auct. jud. Poss. l. fin. D. Tritic. Action. l. 3. §. 3. D. Action. Empt. Bald. Angel. in l. fi fundus. D. Evict. & Bald. in l. quaero. D. Solut. & in Auth. quas actiones Cod. Sacrof. Eccles. Nicol. Everhard. consil. 78. post Cyn. Albericum, de Rosat. Alex. immol. Jason. n. 9. 10.

units.la: de mutuo, n. 15. & in simili. tract. de Auction. libr. 2. c. 4. n. 33. & seqq. Wissenb. disp. Pand. 24. part. 1. vid. Solutas objectiones apud Everh. d consil. n. 30. 40. Gilken. ad l.
units.tr: concerning loans, n. 15, and in a similar case: tract. de Auction. book 2, ch. 4, n. 33 et seq. Wissenbach, disp. Pand. 24, part 1; see the objections answered in Everhard, de consil. n. 30, 40. Gilken, ad l.

units.la: 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n, 23. 24. 25: Vid. & prolixe per omnes casus banc circa contractus materiam deducentem. Gabriel. Comm. opinion. lib. 6. tit. de Consuet. conclus. 1. & 2. ibique II. & DD.
units.tr: 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n, 23. 24. 25: See also the whole of this matter concerning contracts, worked out at length through all the cases. Gabriel. Comm. opinion. lib. 6. tit. de Consuet. conclus. 1. & 2. ibique II. & DD.

units.la: 18. Quid si Curator bonis dandus sit, Debitore forte bonis cedente, vel latitante, vel sine hærede decedente; an conveniendus Judex domicilii debitoris, an bonorum? Respondeo, & si non negavero, uti post dicetur, Judicem domicilii à creditoribus conveniendum esse, si tamen agatur de curatore bonis dando, existumarem eundem quidem dari posse bonis immobilibus, ibidem sitis, non tamen alibi, invito Judice loci. Jussus enim vel praeceptum Judicis, se non extendit ultra limites ejusdem jurisdictionis, Arg. l. alleg. & l. ult. D. Jurisd. l. unic. Cod. Ubi de Possess. l. cum unus. 12. §. is qui possidere. D. de Rebus auctor. Judic. Possid. Gail. 2. obs. 130. n. 13. Mevius ad Lubecens. libr. 3. tit. 1. §. 10. n. 51. Anton. Matth. tractat. de Auction. libr. 1. cap. 7. num. 10. in init. & c. 11. num. 80. in sin.
units.tr: 18. What if a curator must be appointed for the goods, the debtor perhaps having ceded his goods, or gone into hiding, or died without an heir? Must the creditors sue before the judge of the debtor's domicile or before the judge of the goods? I answer, and I will say later that I do not deny it, that the creditors must sue before the judge of the domicile if the matter concerns appointing a curator for the goods. I would think that such a curator can be given for immovable goods lying in that place, but not elsewhere, against the will of the local judge. For the order or command of a judge does not extend beyond the limits of his jurisdiction. Arg. l. alleg. & l. ult. D. Jurisd. l. unic. Cod. Ubi de Possess. l. cum unus. 12. §. is qui possidere. D. de Rebus auctor. Judic. Possid. Gail. 2. obs. 130. n. 13. Mevius ad Lubecens. libr. 3. tit. 1. §. 10. n. 51. Anton. Matth. tractat. de Auction. libr. 1. cap. 7. num. 10. in init. & c. 11. num. 80. in sin.

units.la: 19. Quid si rationes vel à tutore, vel à curatore sint reddendae, scilicet si alibi rationes detulerit, ubi forte domicilium habet, alibi administraverit; an conveniendus ubi domicilium fovet, an ubi administravit? Resp. Affirmatur posterius si modo ibidem reperiatur. Quod ex quasi contractu conveniatur, ad exemplum contractus; per textus expressos in l. 6. in init. l. 4. in sin. D. de Edend. l. 19. §. 1. D. de judic. l. 45. D. eod. l.
units.tr: 19. What if accounts must be rendered either by a guardian or by a curator, for example if he has rendered accounts in one place, where perhaps he has his domicile, but has administered elsewhere? Must he be sued where he has his domicile, or where he administered? The answer is that the latter is affirmed, provided he is found there. He is sued on a quasi-contract, after the model of a contract, by the express texts in l. 6. in init. l. 4. in sin. D. de Edend. l. 19. §. 1. D. de judic. l. 45. D. eod. l.

units.la: Et licet Groeneweg. ad d. l. Cod. Ubi de Ratiocin. nostris & Gallorum moribus post Mornac. Christ. Zypaeum. statuat tutorem rationes reddere teneri coram eo judice, qui eum nominavit, quamvis alio loco tutela gesta sit. id tamen de moribus nostris verum non videtur, per Merul. loc. cit. Negandum tamen non est, quin in loco domicilii, per actorem possit constringi, ut ibidem rationes reddat, modo suis sumptibus actor curet, ut eo rationes, & instrumenta deferantur. d. l. 4. & 6. Covarr. Practic. quaest. 10. n. 4. Vid. Montan. de Tutel. cap. 39. p. 218.
units.tr: And although Groeneweg. ad d. l. Cod. Ubi de Ratiocin. holds, following our customs and those of the French after Mornac and Christophe Zypaeus, that a guardian is bound to render accounts before the judge who appointed him, even though the guardianship was administered in another place, this does not seem true of our customs, according to Merul. loc. cit. Yet it must not be denied that in the place of his domicile he can be compelled by the plaintiff to render his accounts there, provided the plaintiff takes care, at his own expense, that the accounts and documents are brought there. d. l. 4. & 6. Covarr. Practic. quaest. 10. n. 4. Vid. Montan. de Tutel. cap. 39. p. 218.

units.la: Cæterum si de ratiociniis publicis agatur, ad utilitatem publicam spectantibus principaliter; curator vel administrator conveniri poterit in loco ubi administravit, sive ibidem reperiatur, sive non. Quod in tantum procedit, ut remittendus sit ad locum administrationis. l. 2. Cod. ubi Ratiocin. l. sin. Cod. Ubi de Curiali. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. 1. D. de Judic. n. 66. & seqq.
units.tr: Moreover, if the matter concerns public accounts, which chiefly serve the public interest, a curator or administrator may be sued in the place where he administered, whether or not he is found there. This goes so far that he is to be sent back to the place of his administration. l. 2. Cod. ubi Ratiocin. l. sin. Cod. Ubi de Curiali. Barbof. ad l. 19. §. 1. D. de Judic. n. 66. & seqq.

units.la: 20. Quia vero & pupilli & minores quandoque restituuntur, hoc in loco occasionem captabo differendi de Restitutionibus, casu quo statuta variant.
units.tr: 20. Because wards and minors are sometimes also granted restitution, I will take the opportunity in this place to discuss restitutions, in the case where statutes differ.

units.la: In Integrum itaque restitutione petitâ, cujus loci spectandum sit statutum anxie quæritur? Quod ut clarum fiat, declarandum erit ubi petenda sit restitutio; tumque facile colligi poterit, cujus loci statutum veniat considerandum.
units.tr: When restitution in integrum is sought, it is anxiously asked whose statute must be considered? To make this clear, it must be declared where restitution is to be sought; then it can easily be gathered whose place's statute is to be considered.

units.la: Vel itaque in personam agitur, occasione restitutionis, atque adeundus erit judex domicilii ejus, qui convenitur. l. 2. Cod. ubi & apud quem. Barbof. in Collect. ad Cod. eod. tit. ad d. l. 2. per varios ibidem.
units.tr: Either the action is brought against the person on the occasion of restitution, and the judge of the domicile of the person who is sued must be approached. l. 2. Cod. ubi & apud quem. Barbof. in Collect. ad Cod. eod. tit. ad d. l. 2. per varios ibidem.

units.la: Id quod tum procedit, si contractus, cujus ratione in personam agitur, sit perfectus. Ratio in promptu est: contractu quippe persecto, sublata est actio, quæ ex contractu oritur; ut cum ex aliquâ qualitate rescindi quid petitur, nova actio sit intentanda. Quæ tamen cum personalis sit, in foro ejus, qui convenitur instituetur; quod actor sequatur ordinarie forum rei. d. l. 2. Nisi in loco contractus reum reperiat actor, ubi & illum convenire poterit. vid Gaboriel. Comm. opin. concl. 2. n. 7. tit. de Consuet.
units.tr: This holds when the contract on account of which the action is brought against the person has been completed. The reason is ready to hand: once the contract is completed, the action arising from the contract has been extinguished; so when rescission is sought on some ground, a new action must be brought. Yet since this action is personal, it is brought in the forum of the person who is sued, because the plaintiff ordinarily follows the forum of the defendant. d. l. 2. Unless the plaintiff finds the defendant in the place of the contract, where he may also sue him. See Gaboriel. Comm. opin. concl. 2. n. 7. tit. de Consuet.

units.la: Id quod etiam obtinere censent DD. si rescissio petatur implorato judicis officio nobili, uti loquuntur, quod actionis vicem sustinet. c. sin. de offic. judic. Idem etiam obtinere statuunt, si ad ipsum distractum agatur. Quod actione ex contractu perfecto, nequeat agi ad distractum. Ne in unum finem introducta, & inventa, operarentur ejus contrarium. DD. ad l. 1. D. Comm. Divid. Zoes. D. Pro socio. num. sin. vid Oddum de Restit. part. 1. quæst. 32. artic. 13. post Bartol. Bald. Castrens. in l. 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quem.
units.tr: The doctors also hold that this obtains if rescission is sought by invoking the noble office of the judge, as they say, which takes the place of an action. c. sin. de offic. judic. They also lay down that the same obtains if the action is brought for rescission itself. For an action cannot be brought for rescission on the basis of a completed contract; those remedies were introduced and devised for one purpose, and they should not be made to serve the opposite. DD. ad l. 1. D. Comm. Divid. Zoes. D. Pro socio. num. sin. See Oddus de Restit. part. 1. quaest. 32. artic. 13. after Bartolus, Baldus, Castrensis in l. 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quem.

units.la: Excipe de jure Romano nonnullos casus, qui in foro, seu consistorio Principis sunt ventilandi. Ut si petenda restitutio contra libertatem, contra sententiam procuratoris Cæsaris. Vicarii, aut Præfecti urbi, Judicis à Principe dati, contra duplicem sententiam in minorem latam, l. 9. §. ult. junct. l. 10. l. 18. l. 18. §. 1. 2. 4. D. Minor. l. 1. Cod. Ubi & apud quem. l. 3. Cod. Si adverf. Rem. judic. Nov. 113. cap. 1. Azo in summ. Cod. Si sepius in integr. restit. Postul. Cujac, Parat. Cod. Ubi & Apud quem.
units.tr: Under Roman law some cases must be excepted, which are to be argued in the forum or consistory of the Prince: for example, if restitution is sought against liberty, against a sentence of the procurator of Caesar, of the vicar, or of the prefect of the city, or of a judge appointed by the Prince, or against a double sentence pronounced against a minor. l. 9. §. ult. junct. l. 10. l. 18. l. 18. §. 1. 2. 4. D. Minor. l. 1. Cod. Ubi & apud quem. l. 3. Cod. Si adverf. Rem. judic. Nov. 113. cap. 1. Azo in summ. Cod. Si sepius in integr. restit. Postul. Cujac, Parat. Cod. Ubi & Apud quem.

units.la: Quod si contractus sit imperfectus, aget in loco contractus, qui restitui vult, quia etiamnum durat forum contractus. l. in contractibus, §. in omni. Cod. Non. Numer. Pecun.
units.tr: But if the contract is incomplete, one will sue in the place of the contract, the party wishing to be restored, because the forum of the contract still endures. l. in contractibus, §. in omni. Cod. Non. Numer. Pecun.

units.la: Qua etiam ratione, de nullitate contractus in loco contractus agendum esse censent, quod contractum non rite initum fuisse praetendatur. per l. 2. Cod. verb. perfecta. Ubi & apud quem. Bald. in l. praescriptione, num. 15. Cod. Si contra jus. Tessaur. Decis. Pedem. 14. Barbos. ad l. haeres absens. §. proinde. D. de judic. num. 21. 22. 23. & seqq.
units.tr: For the same reason they hold that an action concerning the nullity of a contract is to be brought in the place of the contract, because it is alleged that the contract was not validly entered into. See l. 2. Cod. verb. perfecta. Ubi & apud quem. Bald. in l. praescriptione, num. 15. Cod. Si contra jus. Tessaur. Decis. Pedem. 14. Barbos. ad l. haeres absens. §. proinde. D. de judic. num. 21. 22. 23. & seqq.

units.la: Quam etiam decisionem extendere solent ad casum, quo agitur ad observantiam ipsius contractus, qui nondum est consummatus. Arg. §. 2. instit. de Donat. l. 11. §. 1.
units.tr: They are also accustomed to extend this decision to the case in which one sues for the observance of the contract itself, which is not yet fulfilled. Compare §. 2. instit. de Donat. l. 11. §. 1.

units.la: 2. D. Action. Empt. Bald. Castrens. in l.
units.tr: 2. D. Action. Empt. Bald. Castrens. in l.

units.la: 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quem.
units.tr: 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quem.

units.la: Vel denique agitur in rem actione, idque ad rei restitutionem, tumque petenda restitutio, in loco domicilii ejus, qui convenitur, vel rei sitae. l. 13. §. sin. D. Minor. l. ult. Cod. Ubi in rem actio. Dusren. hoc tit. cap. 3. in sin. & tit. Cod. Ubi & apud quem. Id quod moribus Franciae obtinere, post Rebuff. in tit. de Restit. in integr. num. 19. & 20. & art. art. 1. gloss. 1. num. 40. tenet. Oddus de Restit. quaest. 32. part. 1. artic. 13. n. 116. De nostris moribus idem affirmat. Sanden libr. 1. tit. 15. def. 1. vid. & Mejerum colleg. Argentor. tit. de in integrum Restit. num. 20.
units.tr: Or finally, the action is brought in rem, for the restitution of a thing; and restitution is then sought in the place of the domicile of the person who is sued, or of the place where the thing lies. l. 13. §. sin. D. Minor. l. ult. Cod. Ubi in rem actio. Dusren. hoc tit. cap. 3. in sin. & tit. Cod. Ubi & apud quem. That this obtains under the customs of France, after Rebuff. in tit. de Restit. in integr. num. 19. & 20. & art. art. 1. gloss. 1. num. 40. holds; Oddus de Restit. quaest. 32. part. 1. artic. 13. n. 116. On our customs Sanden libr. 1. tit. 15. def. 1. affirms the same; see also Mejerus colleg. Argentor. tit. de in integrum Restit. num. 20.

units.la: Quid si restitutio petatur adversus sententiam, vel rem judicatam, an petetur à Judice à quo, an potius à Judice ad quem? Resp. prior amplectenda sententia, si aliquid in primo judicio actitatum, contra quod quis velit restitui. Posterior tenenda, si aliquid acciderit in secundo judicio, adversus quod restitui velit actor. Ut tamen secundum DD. coram judice superiori restitutio utroque in casu possit peti. vid. D. Bartol. Bald. in l. praesef. Cod. de Appellat. Capell. Tholos. decis. 393. Aliosque multos apud Oddum de Restitut. part. 1. quaest. 32. artic. 16. per totum.
units.tr: But what if restitution is sought against a sentence or a thing adjudged: is it to be sought from the judge below, or rather from the judge above? The answer: the former view is to be embraced if something was done in the first trial against which one wishes to be restored; the latter is to be held if something has occurred in the second trial against which the plaintiff wishes to be restored. Nevertheless, according to the doctors, restitution may in either case be sought before the superior judge. See D. Bartol. Bald. in l. praesef. Cod. de Appellat. Capell. Tholos. decis. 393. And many others cited by Oddus de Restitut. part. 1. quaest. 32. artic. 16. throughout.

units.la: Assignavi locum judicii, qui spectandus, assignandum statutum, quod respicere judicem oportet in judicando. Vel itaq; agitur in ipsa restitutione de iis negotiis, quae contractus spectant solemnia, vel quae causae momentum, id est, ipsum contractum. Si prius, sic ut quis restitui velit propter solemnia in contractu non servata, unde grande damnum pateretur, restituetur ex generali clausula ex forma statuti, ubi contractus erat celebratus. Arg. l. 1. in sin. D. ex quibus causa. Major. l. 6. D. Eviction. Alexand. 2. consil. 37. n. 3.
units.tr: I have indicated the place of judgment that must be considered, and the statute that the judge must look to when judging. Now, in the restitution itself, the matter concerns either the formalities of the contract or the substance of the cause, that is, the contract itself. If it is the former, and someone wishes to be restored because formalities in the contract were not observed, and he would suffer great loss as a result, he will be restored under the general clause of the statute's form where the contract was made. Arg. l. 1. in sin. D. ex quibus causa. Major. l. 6. D. Eviction. Alexand. 2. consil. 37. n. 3.

units.la: Quid si restitui velit, propter damnum ex ipso contractu proveniens, tunc erit restituendus, non secundum statutum loci, in quem destinata est solutio, sed loci celebrati contractus, si modo ibidem causa sit data distractus, seu restitutionis. Bartol. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 20. 28. Mascard. conclus. 7. n. 36. de Statutor. interpret.
units.tr: But if someone wishes to be restored because of loss arising from the contract itself, he is to be restored not according to the statute of the place to which payment is destined, but according to the statute of the place where the contract was made, provided the cause of the dissolution or restitution arose there. Bartol. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 20. 28. Mascard. conclus. 7. n. 36. de Statutor. interpret.

units.la: Quod si quis ex post facto restitui velit, qui laesus est, vel per moram, vel negligentiam, servabitur loci statutum, ubi illa mora vel negligentia est contracta vel commissa. Modo ibidem reperiatur reus, vel de moribus sistatur. Bartol. ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 20. Bald. ibid. n. 94. DD. in l. 2. D. de eo quod certo loco dari oport. & inc. licet de foro competent. Mascard. d. tract. conclus. 7. n. 55.
units.tr: But if someone who has been harmed wishes to be restored afterwards, on account of delay or negligence, the statute of the place where that delay or negligence was incurred or committed will be observed, provided the defendant is found there, or can be brought to appear there by his manner of life. Bartol. ad l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 20. Bald. ibid. n. 94. DD. in l. 2. D. de eo quod certo loco dari oport. & inc. licet de foro competent. Mascard. d. tract. conclus. 7. n. 55.

units.la: Ut hic statutum loci, coincidat cum statuto loci ubi judicium acceptum, secundum quod facienda restitutio. l. 22. in sin. D. Rebus Credit. Mynsing. 4. obs. 82. Gilken. ad tit. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 55. Gothefred. ad l.
units.tr: So here the statute of the place coincides with the statute of the place where the judgment was received, according to which the restitution is to be made. l. 22. in sin. D. Rebus Credit. Mynsing. 4. obs. 82. Gilken. ad tit. Cod. Summ. Trinit. n. 55. Gothefred. ad l.

units.la: 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quos.
units.tr: 2. Cod. Ubi & apud quos.

units.la: Quod si agatur de restitutione in rem, quae immobilis, idem dicendum; scilicet, statutum judicii coincidere, cum statuto rei sitae. Adeoque in causae decisione, rei sitae statutum esse spectandum. Si de re mobili spectandum esse statutum domicilii ejus, qui convenitur, quod mobilia personam comitentur, & ubi persona domicilium fovet, esse intelligantur. Utrtamen res mobiles, si sit in bona fide reus, sint deferendæ ad ejus domicilii locum, idque sumptibus petitoris, qui extra cibaria in iter & navigationem sunt faciendi. l. 10. D. Rei vindic. Except. cajub. l. 11. 12, D. eod. Quæ omnia ex ante dictis, & post dicendis, notiora sunt, quam ut hic prolixiore egeant declaratione. vid. Prolixæ Barbos. ad l. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 24. 25. 26. & seqq. Covarr. 1, Resol. 4. & 2, Resol. 12. Fabrum in Cod. de legibus. desin. 2. 4. Treutler, disput. de Restit. in integr. ibique Bachov. Berlichium, 1. decis. 6. Zoes. D. vulg. Subst. n. 29.
units.tr: If the action concerns restitution in respect of an immovable thing, the same is to be said: namely, that the statute of the judgment coincides with the statute of the place where the thing lies. Accordingly, in deciding the case, the statute of the place where the thing lies is to be observed. If the thing is movable, the statute of the domicile of the defendant is to be observed, since movables follow the person and are understood to be where the person has his domicile. Nevertheless, if the defendant is in good faith, the movables are to be carried to the place of his domicile, at the expense of the plaintiff, who must bear the costs of the journey and shipping beyond the cost of maintenance. l. 10. D. Rei vindic. Except. cajub. l. 11. 12. D. eod. All these points are better known from what has been said before and what is still to be said than they need a lengthier explanation here. See Barbosa at length on l. 19. §. proinde. D. judic. n. 24. 25. 26. & seqq. Covarr. 1. Resol. 4. & 2. Resol. 12. Fabrum in Cod. de legibus. desin. 2. 4. Treutler, disput. de Restit. in integr. and there Bachov. Berlichius, 1. decis. 6. Zoes. D. vulg. Subst. n. 29.

units.la: 21. Quid si mulier restitui velit adversus dotem marito datam, spectandum ne statutum loci domicilii præsentis mariti, an domicilii mariti, quod erat tempore soluti matrimonii? Respondeo, spectandum statutum mariti domicilii præsentis, maxime si ea intentione contractum matrimonium, ut ibi perpetuo habitarent.
units.tr: 21. What if a wife wishes to be restored against a dowry given to her husband: is the statute of the domicile of the husband at present to be considered, or the statute of the husband's domicile that existed at the time the marriage was dissolved? I answer: the statute of the husband's present domicile is to be considered, especially if the marriage was contracted with the intention that they would live there permanently.

units.la: Si tamen aliquo facto, aut culpa mariti solutum matrimonium, etiam spectari poterit novum mariti domicilium, in quantum illud spectari, interest uxoris. Arg. l. 22. in sin. D. Rebus. credit.
units.tr: If, however, the marriage was dissolved through some act or fault of the husband, his new domicile may also be considered, insofar as it is in the wife's interest that it be considered. Arg. l. 22. in sin. D. Rebus. credit.

units.la: Quemadmodum etiam novum spectatur domicilium, si uxor duxerit maritum ad suam domum; si domicilium sine mariti culpa sit mutatum; vel non fraudandi uxoris gratia; tiâ; vel immobilia in dotem data, alibi sita. Regulæ propositæ ratio est, quod ubi de restitutione dotis intentanda actio, ibi etiam videatur adversus dotem mulier esse restituenda. Argum. l. heres absens. § sin. D. de Re judic. l. 65. D. de judic. ubi DD. l. unic. Cod. Si adversus dotem. Roeland. à Valle de lucro dot. q 13. 20. Bald. in l. voluntas. in Princ. Cod. fideicomm. & Consil. 208. vol. 3. aliique qui diss. apud Mascard. de statut. interpret. conclus. 7. n. 57. 58. 59. & seqq. usque ad n. 72. qui quia satis accuratus, malui lectorem eo remittere, quam ut ipsius probe dicta, mea faciam, aut rapsodum agam.
units.tr: In the same way, a new domicile is also taken into account if the wife has brought her husband to her own home; if the domicile was changed without the husband's fault; or not in order to defraud the wife; likewise, or if immovable property given in dowry is situated elsewhere. The reason for the stated rule is that where the action for recovery of the dowry is to be brought, there too the wife seems to be bound to be restored against the dowry. Argument from l. heres absens, § sin, D. de re judicata; l. 65, D. de judiciis; the Doctors on l. unica, Cod. si adversus dotem; Roland à Valle, de lucro dotis, q. 13, n. 20; Bald. on l. voluntas, in princ., Cod. de fideicommissis; and Consilium 208, vol. 3; and others who discuss it, cited in Mascardus, De statutis et eorum interpretatione, conclusio 7, nn. 57–59 and following, up to n. 72. Since he is accurate enough, I preferred to refer the reader to him rather than make their well-expressed words my own or play the rhapsodist.

units.la: SECTIO DECIMA.
units.tr: SECTION TEN.

units.la: CAPUT UNICUM.
units.tr: THE ONE CHAPTER.

units.la: 1. Si statuta varient circa actionum terminos, quæ spectanda?
units.tr: 1. If statutes differ concerning the time limits of actions, which are to be regarded?

units.la: 2. Si intentandæ actiones personales, quale statutum spectandum?
units.tr: 2. If personal actions are to be brought, which statute is to be regarded?

units.la: 3. Si debitor a pluribus creditoribus conveniendus, ubi concursus judicium sit formandus, si particulare.
units.tr: 3. If a debtor is to be sued by several creditors, where is the concursus judgment to be constituted, if it is a particular one?

units.la: 4. Quid si judicium sit universale, puta in cessione bonorum, beneficio intentarii &c.? 5. Quid si creditorum unus per hypothecam sibi prospexerit abunde?
units.tr: 4. What if the judgment is universal, as in cession of goods, the benefit of inventory, etc.? 5. What if one of the creditors has provided amply for himself by a mortgage?

units.la: 6. Cujus loci servanda solemnia circa procedendi modum?
units.tr: 6. Whose place's solemnities are to be observed regarding the mode of proceeding?

units.la: 7. Circa ferias variantes?
units.tr: 7. Regarding differing holidays?

units.la: 8. Circa cautiones?
units.tr: 8. Regarding securities?

units.la: 9. Circa probationes?
units.tr: 9. Regarding proofs?

units.la: 10. Circa editionem instrumentorum?
units.tr: 10. Regarding the production of documents?

units.la: 11. Utrum instrumentum per notarium in uno loco factum, alibi vires exferat?
units.tr: 11. Whether an instrument made by a notary in one place has force elsewhere?

units.la: 12. Si sententia proferenda, quae solemnia servanda?
units.tr: 12. If a sentence is to be pronounced, which solemnities are to be observed?

units.la: 13. Si causae merita examinanda, quodnam spectandum statutum?
units.tr: 13. If the merits of the case are to be examined, which statute is to be regarded?

units.la: 14. Circa executionem tum ratione causae, tum solemnium, quae spectanda statuta?
units.tr: 14. Regarding execution, both as to the cause and as to the solemnities, which statutes are to be regarded?

units.la: 15. Si circa appellationem contentio, an statutum judicis à quo, an ad quem, spectandum erit?
units.tr: 15. If the dispute concerns an appeal, is the statute of the judge a quo or of the judge ad quem to be regarded?

units.la: 16. Quis judex spectandus ratione citationis?
units.tr: 16. Which judge is to be regarded with respect to citation?

units.la: 1. VErum quia post restitutiones de jure civili sequitur materia judiciaria, concursum statutorum circa eandem hic examinare decrevi. Ubi quoad actionis intentationem, occurrit illa difficultas, an si diversa sint statuta circa actionis finitionem seu terminum, spectandus sit terminus statuti debitoris, an creditoris? Respondeo, quia actor sequitur forum rei, ideo extraneus petens a reo, quod sibi debetur, sequetur terminum statuti praescriptum actioni in foro rei. Et quia hoc statutum non exserit vires extra territorium statuentis, ideo, etiam reo alibi convento, tale statutum objicere non poterit. per all. super. vid. Gabriel. commun. conclus. libr. 6. conclus. 11.
units.tr: 1. But since, after restitutions in civil law, the matter of judicial procedure follows, I have decided to examine here the conflict of statutes concerning it. Here, as regards the bringing of an action, the difficulty arises: if statutes differ concerning the limitation or term of the action, is the term of the debtor's statute to be regarded, or that of the creditor's? I answer: since the plaintiff follows the forum of the defendant, a foreigner who sues a defendant for what is owed to him will follow the time limit prescribed for the action in the forum of the defendant. And because this statute does not exert force outside the territory of the one who enacted it, the defendant cannot object such a statute even if he is sued elsewhere. See the all. super.; see Gabriel, Communes conclusiones, book 6, conclusion 11.

units.la: 2. Quid si actiones sint intentandae & quidem personales, an sequemur, statutum domicilii debitoris, an statutum loci, ubi exigi vel intentari poterunt? Respondeo, etsi bene multi velint tales actiones certo loco non circumscribi, inspecta tantum illa corporali circumscriptione, ut tamen eas velint censeri de loco ubi agi & exigi possunt, Alexand. consil. 16. in sin. vol. 1. Tiraquell. de Retract. §. 36. gloss 3. n. 16. 17. & de jure primogen. q. 49. n. 6. Tessaur. quaest. forens. libr. 2. q. 5. n. 15. 16. Cravett. consil. 934. n. 11.
units.tr: 2. What if actions are to be brought, and indeed personal ones: shall we follow the statute of the debtor's domicile, or the statute of the place where they can be demanded or brought? I answer: although many wish such actions not to be confined to a certain place, looking only at that bodily confinement, yet they wish them to be deemed to be of the place where they can be pursued and demanded: Alexander, consil. 16, at the end, vol. 1; Tiraquellus, de Retractu, §36, gloss 3, nn. 16, 17, and de jure primogeniorum, q. 49, n. 6; Tessaurus, Quaestiones forenses, book 2, q. 5, nn. 15, 16; Cravetta, consil. 934, n. 11.

units.la: Quia tamen mobilibus annumerantur, sic ut loco non circumscribantur. l. quaesitum. 12. §. Papinianus D. de fund. instruct. l. uxorem. 39. §. legaverat. l. quaesitum. 76. §. 1. l. Similiter Mævia. 90. D. legat. 3. l. Cajus Sejus. 88. D. leg. 2. Etiam domicilium & personam debitoris, adeoque ejusdem loci statutum respiciunt. Æs quippe alienum personale, universum debitoris patrimonium respicit. Non aliter atque divisâ bonorum administratione, licet in diversis provinciis, jus individuum permanet. l. 50. §. 1. D. de judic. l. inter tutores D. Admin. Tutor. l. 1. Cod. de divis. Tutel. Bartol. in d. l. 50. Salicet. in l. 1. Cod. Summ. Trinit. Peregrin. de Jure fisc. libr. 5. tit. 1. n. 144. Montan. de Tutel. c. 39. n. 109. & c. 32 n. 104. Salgado de Somosa labyrinth. concurs. creditor. part. 2. c. 12. n. 21. & seqq. vid. & Choppin. de Moribus Paris. libr. 2. tit. 5. n. 20. 21.
units.tr: Yet because they are counted among movables, so that they are not confined to a place: l. quaesitum 12, §Papinianus, D. de fundo instructo; l. uxorem 39, §legaverat; l. quaesitum 76, §1; l. Similiter Mævia 90, D. legat. 3; l. Cajus Seius 88, D. legat. 2. They also regard the domicile and person of the debtor, and therefore the statute of his place. For a personal debt concerns the debtor's whole estate, just as, even when the administration of goods is divided between different provinces, the right remains undivided: l. 50, §1, D. de judiciis; l. inter tutores, D. administratione tutorum; l. 1, Cod. de divisione tutelae; Bartolus on l. 50; Salicetus on l. 1, Cod. Summa Trinitas; Peregrinus, de jure fisci, book 5, tit. 1, n. 144; Montanus, de tutela, c. 39, n. 109, and c. 32, n. 104; Salgado de Somoza, Labyrinthus creditorum concurrentium, part 2, c. 12, nn. 21 ff.; see also Choppin, de moribus Parisiensibus, book 2, tit. 5, nn. 20, 21.

units.la: 3. Occasione praecedentis difficultatis, unam atque alteram subjungam, non prorsus ab hac alienam materia. Quid si creditores in diversis habitantes territoriis, debitorem in diversis conveniant tribunalibus; an in uno concurrere debebunt, an potius singuli recte in suis tribunalibus conveniant debitorem, idque vel ratione contractus, vel ratione mobilium ibidem repertorum? Respondeo, si unus creditorum aliquid petat à debitore, & judicio pendente, alii creditores coram eodem tribunali compareant, qui se jure potiori gaudere contendant, dubium nullum, quin omnes, coram illo judice, coram quo prior egit creditor, agere debeant. Quod semel volentes judici non suo subjecerint. l. 1. & 1. & 2. in init. D. de Judic. Nec tamen hoc judicium erit universale, ut alibi creditoribus existentibus, qui sese non opposuerunt, præjudicet. Quamobrem alibi debitorem convenire poterunt, idque vel ratione contractus, vel mobilium nomine; sic ut priorem judicem, ab aliis jam aditum creditoribus, eligere non teneantur. Hinc quia nulla est connexio causæ, sententia quæ à priori judice lata est, neque extra territorium alteri præjudicium adferre poterit. Prolixe post Giurbam consil. 46. & Parlador. 2. Rer. quot. 9. Salgad. de Somosa labyrint. concurs. creditor. p. 1. c. 4. §. 1. ubi etiam accurate varios describit modos, quibus causæ dicantur connexæ, aut continentes. n. 43. & seqq.
units.tr: 3. Occasioned by the preceding difficulty, I will add one or two more, not wholly foreign to this matter. What if creditors living in different territories sue the debtor in different courts: must they concur in one, or may each rightly sue the debtor in his own court, whether by reason of a contract or by reason of movables found there? I answer: if one of the creditors seeks something from the debtor, and while the case is pending other creditors appear before the same court, contending that they have a stronger right, there is no doubt that all must sue before that judge before whom the first creditor acted, since they have once voluntarily submitted themselves to a judge who is not their own: l. 1, and l. 1 and 2 in init., D. de judiciis. Nor, however, will this judgment be universal so as to prejudice creditors existing elsewhere who have not joined themselves to it. Accordingly they may sue the debtor elsewhere, whether by reason of a contract or on account of movables, so that they are not bound to choose the prior judge, already approached by the other creditors. Hence, since there is no connexion of cause, a sentence given by the prior judge cannot bring prejudice to another outside his territory. See at length, after Giurba, consil. 46, and Parlador, 2 Rer. quot. 9; Salgado de Somoza, Labyrinthus creditorum concurrentium, part 1, c. 4, §1, where he also accurately describes the various modes by which causes are said to be connected or continent: nn. 43 ff.

units.la: 4. Quod si judicium concursus creditorum sit universale, quale erit judicium cessionis impetratæ, obtenti beneficii inventarii &c. & quidem debitor judicium concursus formaverit coram suo judice, omnes creditores coram eodem judice concurrere tenebuntur. Etsi alio debitorem traxerint, exceptionem objiciet continentiæ causæ, & quidem ante litem contestatam. Ratio jam dicta est, ne continentia causæ dividatur; neve causæ diversæ apud diversos judices absurdū producant, & singulæ diversas aut contrarias sententias consequantur. l. 1. 2. D. de quibus rebus ad eundem judicem. l. nulli. Cod. judic. l. Si idem. §. quid si. D. de jurisd. l. 1. Cod. Aff. tollend.
units.tr: 4. But if the judgment of the concourse of creditors is universal, as is a judgment of an obtained cession, of the benefit of inventory, etc., and indeed if the debtor has constituted the concursus judgment before his own judge, all the creditors will be bound to concur before that same judge. Even if they have dragged the debtor elsewhere, he will raise the exception of continence of cause, and indeed before the litis contestation. The reason has already been stated: that the continence of the cause may not be divided, and that separate causes before different judges may not produce absurdity, with each reaching a different or contrary sentence: l. 1, 2, D. de quibus rebus ad eundem judicem; l. nulli, Cod. de judiciis; l. Si idem, §quid si, D. de jurisdictione; l. 1, Cod. Aff. tollend.

units.la: tollend. Arg. l. 44. D. Religios. à simili. Socinus, Bartol. Bald. Alexand. Covarr. pract. q. 36. n. 1. 2. Tiraquell. in l. si unquam. Cod. Revoc. Donat. n. 192. Gail. 2. obs. 130. & innumeri apud Salgado de Somosa. labyrinth. concurs. creditor, part. 1. c. 4. n. 15. 16. 17. 18. & seqq. & d. c. 4. §. 2. 3. Rodenb. de jure conjug. tit. 2. c. 5. n. 15. p. 92.
